ASSAULT ON RICSHA COOLIE BY JAPANESE

At 10.30 p.m. yesterday, a Japanese, in front of a certain Japanese wine shop at the corner of Haining and Woosung Roads, hired ricsha No. 38973 pulled by coolie named Sung Ying-tsung (沈迎春) to take him to Kungping Road near Yochow Road.
At the destination, the coolie asked for the fare, but the Japanese refused payment. A dispute ensued, whereupon the Japanese forcibly drew the coolie into an umbrella factory, a Japanese concern, closed the door and assaulted him. Another Japanese also took part in the assault.
Hearing the cries of the coolie for help, neighbours came, but could not enter the factory owing to the door being shut. The matter was reported to Wayside Police Station and detectives were sent to make an investigation. The injured coolie was removed to the Sacred Heart Hospital for treatment.

Kuo Min (國民) Weekly, Vol. 1, Issue No. 10 :-

SETTLEMENT FILM AND DRAMATIC CENSORSHIP

In order to please the Japanese, the authorities of the foreign Settlements in Shanghai have unreasonably interfered with the patriotic movements of the Chinese people since the January 28 Incident in 1931. For instance, any Chinese film which suggests national defence or contains maps referring to the North-East is either subject to cuts or to banning from exhibition in the foreign Settlements. Even a song or a dramatic play which contains absolutely no anti-Japanese sentiments but mentions only that China should strengthen herself is banned from singing or exhibition. However, in the case of "The New Earth", a film of Japanese production which advocates invasion of China, the Settlement authorities allowed exhibition in their jurisdiction. Such action on the part of the Settlement authorities is unfair.
With a view to pushing forward the boycott movement on smuggled goods, the Shanghai Various Circles' Smuggled Goods Boycott Movement Committee recently requested assistance from various cinemas in propagating the movement by showing lantern slides containing slogans on the boycott of smuggled goods before each performance was given. Fearing that the Japanese might present representations to them, the Settlement authorities prohibited the exhibition of these lantern slides. It is really unreasonable to interfere with such a movement as the boycott of smuggled goods.
Thus, we are of the opinion that the demand of certain public organizations in Shanghai to withdraw the right of censorship of films and dramatic plays in the foreign Settlements is proper and reasonable. We hope that the Chinese authorities will pay close attention to this problem and will devise ways and means to arrive at this aim at an early date.

《国民》周刊，第一卷第十期：

租界电影及戏剧审查

为了取悦日本人，上海外国租界当局自 1931 年一·二八事变以来，一直无理干涉中国人的爱国运动。例如，任何暗示国防或包含涉及东北地图的中国电影，要么被删剪，要么被禁止在外国租界放映。甚至一首歌或一出戏剧，只要其中完全没有反日情绪，而仅仅提到中国应当自强，也被禁止演唱或演出。然而，对于日本制作的宣扬侵华的电影《新土》，租界当局却允许在其辖区内放映。租界当局的这种行为是不公平的。
为了推进抵制走私货物运动，上海各界抵制走私货物运动委员会最近请求各家电影院协助宣传该运动，即在每场演出前放映含有抵制走私货物标语的幻灯片。租界当局担心日本人可能会向他们提出交涉，因此禁止放映这些幻灯片。干涉抵制走私货物这样的运动，实在是不合理的。
因此，我们认为上海某些公共团体要求收回外国租界对电影和戏剧的审查权是正当且合理的。我们希望中国当局密切关注这一问题，并设法早日实现这一目标。

Chun Chung Sin Wan (群众新闻) publishes the following article
written by one Ping Tseu (平舟) :-

ARROGANT BEHAVIOUR OF "FRIENDLY PEOPLE" IN SHANGHAI AS
IN NORTH-EAST

Shanghai still belongs to China, yet we may
see in Hongkew our enemy's same beast-like actions as in
North China. The barbarous acts of the people of our
"friendly nation" in Shanghai have become daily occurrences.
For instance, they never pay ricksha fares but make the
coolie feel their fists instead.
At nightfall yesterday, I was taking a walk
on Dixwell Road. I saw five or six people of our "friendly
nation" wearing wooden clogs and Kimono, surround a hawker
and buy some glass cups. They did not ask the price,
but went away with the cups after paying a few coppers.
The hawker became angry and began to abuse them, saying
"Do you all want to rob me?" One of the people of our
"friendly nation" rushed forward and gave the hawker two
slaps on the face and a kick. A crowd of spectators had
gathered by this time, but they did not interfere.
One of the spectators said: "Hawker, go away
quickly. It will do you no good to quarrel with them".
Upon this, the hawker left. I also left in anger although
I had intended to speak.
At the Kashing Road Bridge, I could bear it
no longer and said to the hawker: "We should devise ways
and means to avenge the hurt you received a moment ago from
the Japanese". The hawker turned his head to look at
me, nodded assent and left.
I could not help reflecting that although
Shanghai is not in the North-East, yet conditions similar
to those in the North-East are prevalent here. We should
not merely use the slogan "Shanghai is ours and the North-
East is ours", but we should endeavour to bring it about
in fact.

“友邦人士”在上海如在东北般傲慢

上海仍属于中国，但我们却在虹口看到了敌人在华北同样的兽行。我们“友邦”人士在上海的野蛮行径已成为日常 occurrences（原文如此，意为常事）。例如，他们从不付人力车费，反而让车夫尝尝他们的拳头。
昨天黄昏时分，我在狄思威路散步。我看见五六个穿着木屐和和服的“友邦”人士围住一个小贩，买了一些玻璃杯。他们没有问价，只付了几个铜板就拿着杯子走了。小贩很生气，开始骂他们，说：“你们都想抢劫我吗？”其中一名“友邦”人士冲上前，给了小贩两记耳光并踢了一脚。此时已聚集了一群围观者，但他们并未介入。
一名围观者说：“小贩，快走吧。跟他们吵架对你没好处。”
于是，小贩离开了。虽然我本想说话，但也愤怒地离开了。
在嘉善路桥，我再也无法忍受，对小贩说：“我们应该想办法为你刚才受日本人的伤害报仇。”小贩转过头看着我，点头表示同意，然后离开了。
我不禁反思，虽然上海不在东北，但类似东北的情况在这里却很普遍。我们不应仅仅使用“上海是我们的，东北也是我们的”这一口号，而应努力使其成为事实。

Sin Wan Pao published on January 24 the following letter (dated
January 3) sent by one Chang Ping Chong (張炳章) to the
editor :-

A TRAGEDY

At about 3 p.m. yesterday (January 2) I saw four
XX at the corner of Woochang and Chapoc Roads. Three of
them were in foreign dress and one in student's uniform, all
were drunk. One who was wearing a yellow overcoat suddenly
struck a scavenger on the face. The scavenger was about to
retaliate but, as soon as he realized that the one who
struck him was a XX, he ran into an alleyway. The rabid
dog with the yellow overcoat then became madder and began to
strike and kick every Chinese pedestrian he could see.
At that time a Cantonese who was wearing a grey
cloth jacket and cap, was walking eastwards along Woochang
Road. He was unexpectedly caught by the yellow rabid dog
and severely beaten. He attempted to resist, but the four
XX overpowered him, threw him to the ground and punched him.
The Cantonese cried for help. There were many Chinese
on-lookers but none of them dared to help him. Finally,
one of the XX, who was comparatively sober, stopped his
comrades from further assaulting the Cantonese. Our
fellow countryman got up and tried to argue with the XX,
but received several kicks for his pains. The XX then made
their way along Woochang Road and the spectators dispersed.
The four XX might have assaulted others because
they were drunk; there were many foreigners on the road
and they were not assaulted. Is this not an insult to
the Chinese people?
During the assault, a Chinese policeman stood
in front of a shop at some distance away and watched the
fracas without making an attempt to save his own countryman.
A child of about 12 or 13 years old asked him why he did
not go to help the Chinese and the policeman said, "The
Police have no power to deal with the XX when they have done
anything wrong."
What does this mean? We Chinese live in
the Settlement and pay taxes. Are we not entitled to
protection when we are walking on the road? Suppose
that the Chinese had been beaten to death, would the Police
have done nothing about it? When a XX is killed, they
will at once create trouble and extort money from us, but
when we are insulted in our own territory, we cannot have
our wrongs redressed. How distressful is all this!
I send you this letter in order to show how
the nationals of our friendly nation treat us. I
assure you that what I have said is true and shall be obliged
if you will publish this letter.

1 月 24 日出版的《新闻报》刊登了一封由张炳章于 1 月 3 日写给编辑的信：

一场悲剧

昨天（1 月 2 日）下午 3 点左右，我在武昌路与乍浦路转角处看到四个 XX（原文不清，推测指外国人/日本人）。其中三人穿西装，一人穿学生制服，全都喝醉了。其中一个穿着黄色大衣的人突然打了一名清道夫的脸。清道夫正要还手，但当他意识到打他的是一个 XX 时，便跑进了一条弄堂。那个穿着黄色大衣的疯狗变得更加疯狂，开始殴打和踢踹他看到的每一个中国行人。
当时，一个穿着灰色布夹克和帽子的广东人正沿着武昌路向东走。他意外地被那只黄色的疯狗抓住并遭到毒打。他试图反抗，但这四个 XX 制服了他，将他摔倒在地并拳打脚踢。广东人呼救。周围有许多中国围观者，但无人敢帮助他。最后，其中一个比较清醒的 XX 阻止了他的同伴继续殴打该广东人。我们的同胞站起来试图与 XX 理论，结果却挨了几脚。随后，这四个 XX 沿着武昌路离去，围观者也散开了。
这四个 XX 可能是因为喝醉了才殴打他人；路上有很多外国人，但他们并未受到攻击。这难道不是对中国人的侮辱吗？
在殴打过程中，一名中国警察站在远处的一家商店前，看着这场混乱，却没有试图救助自己的同胞。一个大约十二三岁的孩子问他为什么不去帮助中国人，警察说：“当 XX 做错事时，警察无权管治他们。”
这意味着什么？我们中国人住在租界，纳税。我们在路上行走时难道无权得到保护吗？假如中国人被打死，警察会无动于衷吗？当一个 XX 被杀时，他们立刻就会制造麻烦并向我们勒索钱财，但当我们在自己的领土上受到侮辱时，却无法伸冤。这是多么令人悲痛啊！
我寄这封信是为了展示我们友邦的国民是如何对待我们的。我保证我所说的是真实的，如果您能刊登这封信，我将不胜感激。

Ta Chia Kan (大家看), a bi-weekly periodical, published the following article in its first issue dated November 10:-

THE CASE OF CHEN KWEI YUNG, A PEANUT HAWKER.

The other day, the marines of a certain nation constructed defence works in the rear of Hua Yuen Ka (花園街), Chapei. A peanut hawker named Chen Kwei Yung (陳桂榮), who was passing by the place, was stopped by these marines and held up like a prisoner.
The marines said to him:- "The work on the military defence here is very urgent. We are converting the place into a military barracks, but we lack coolies to transport stones. During the past few days, the residents of Chapei have confined themselves indoors and it is difficult to get men to do the work. It seems that you have come out to secure military information. If you are really a law-abiding person and a hawker, you must do the coolie work for us. When fighting takes place between X and China, we, the people of X nation, will already have a large number of troops in Chapei".
Chen Kwei Yung replied:- "I am a citizen of China and will not transport stones for you. Do not falsely accuse me. I will not work for the enemy".
The marines of X nation became very angry upon hearing his reply and abused him, saying :- "You, Chinese slave. Ninety per cent of China has been ruined. You should surrender and submit to us; thus you may save your life".
Chen Kwei Yung became angry and said:- "Who will surrender to you?"
The marines of X nation then stabbed him with bayonets and Chen ran away, crying for help. The marines chased him, but could not overtake him. Only his ears were wounded and bled.
Brethren! We must seek revenge, otherwise we shall soon become slaves.

花生小贩陈桂荣案。

Shun Pao and other local newspapers:-
A BURGLAR'S FALSE ALLEGATION AGAINST JAPANESE
According to a report published in the "Hwa
Mei Wan Pao" on October 17, one Zung Kwei Yoong (陳桂榮)
native of Nanzing (南 潯), was stabbed by a Japanese marine
in the left ear. In connection with this case, a section of
the public distributed handbills to express their indignation.
A reporter of the Central News Agency now
learns that according to investigations made by the Bureau
of Public Safety and the Shanghai Municipal Police, Zung Kwei
Yoong received the injury to his left ear when he was caught
by the tenant in the act of entering a dwelling house in
Chapei with the intention of committing a burglary. He
managed to escape and went to the Paulun Hospital for treat-
ment. Fearing that if he told the truth about his injury,
the hospital authorities would report to the Police, he told
them a fabricated story that he had been attacked by Japanese.
The hospital authorities referred the matter to the Police
and this gave rise to the misleading reports. Subsequent
investigations showed that the man's story was absolutely
false and that he was a habitual offender, his arm having
been marked with the brand of a criminal.

ACCorDing to a report published in the "Hwa

learns that according to investigations made by the Bureau
of Public Safety and the Shanghai Municipal Police, Zung Kwei
Yoong received the injury to his left ear when he was caught

investigations showed that the man's story was absolutely
false and that he was a habitual offender, his arm having
been marked with the brand of a criminal.

Peanut Vendor Tells Wild
Tale To Prevent His Arrest

Settlement, Chinese Police Inquiry Reveals
Hawker In Scuffle After Burglary

Further investigation of the case in which a peanut vendor,
Chen Kwei-yung, charged that he was bayonetted by a member of the
Japanese Naval Landing Party, showed yesterday that Chen had
told the story to the Paulun Hospital officials and the Sinza Police
in order to avoid detection of his attempt to burglarize a house in
Chapel.

At the time when Chen told his version, claiming his ear was
sliced by a bluejacket, he was believed by both the police and the
hospital authorities. His story was thus released to the press through
usually authentic channels.

Later inquiry conducted by the Settlement and the Chinese po-
lice, however, indicated that the self-styled peanut vendor had tried
to commit a theft in a house in Chapel. Tenants of the house at-
tempted to arrest him. In the scuffle, Chen's ear was injured.

Knowing that if he had told the true version of his story to the
police and the hospital officials, it would mean his arrest and pro-
bably punishment, Chen apparently fabricated the story of the at-
tack.

After exhaustive investigation, police officials were last night able
to say that Chen's original story was groundless.

花生小贩编造荒诞故事以逃避逮捕

租界与华警调查揭示
小贩在入室盗窃未遂后发生冲突

对花生小贩陈桂荣指控被日本海军特别陆战队成员用刺刀刺伤一案的进一步调查，于昨日显示，陈桂荣向宝隆医院官员和新闸捕房讲述该故事，是为了避免其在Chapel（原文如此，应为Chapei/闸北）一处住宅企图入室盗窃的行为被发现。

当陈桂荣讲述其版本，声称其耳朵被一名水兵割伤时，警方和医院当局均信以为真。因此，他的故事通过通常可靠的渠道发布给了新闻界。

然而，随后由租界和华人警察进行的调查表明，这名自称花生小贩的人曾试图在Chapel（原文如此，应为Chapei/闸北）的一处住宅内行窃。该住宅的租户试图逮捕他。在扭打中，陈桂荣的耳朵受伤。

陈桂荣显然知道，如果向警方和医院官员讲述真实情况，将意味着他被逮捕并可能受到惩罚，因此编造了遭袭击的故事。

经过详尽调查，警方官员于昨晚表示，陈桂荣最初的说法毫无根据。

JAPANESE PROTEST
AGAINST PAPERS

Story of Wounding Said to be
Absolutely False

Alleged false reports of a bayonet
wound inflicted upon the ear of a
Chinese peanut vendor by a Japanese
bluejacket will form the subject of
stern representations to be made
with the local Chinese authorities by
the Japanese, the Shanghai "Nippo"
reported yesterday. A spokesman of
the Special Naval Landing Party told
Domei last night that the published
report was absolutely incorrect. Had
such an incident taken place, it
would immediately have been re-
ported to the headquarters of the
Landing Party. No such report has
been made.

Inquiries made by the Landing
Party with the Shanghai Municipal
Police and the Chinese Public Safety
Bureau, the officer asserted, elicited
firm denials of the incident from both.
It had been stated that Chen Kwei-
ying, a Chapel peanut vendor, was
drafted by several Japanese blue-
jackets to carry stones near the in-
tersection of North Szechuen and
Dixwell Roads. Tired, the man
abandoned work and resumed selling
his wares. Then, a Japanese blue-
jacket approached the man and
lunged at him with the bayonet. The
thrust missed his face, but slashed
his ear. The wounded man was
taken to the Paojun Hospital, where
he was given treatment, and then
reported to the Dixwell Road Police
Station. The latter immediately
turned over the matter to the Chinese
Public Safety Bureau.

This report, the "Nippo" declared,
was absolutely false, and merely a
piece of "wilful demagoguery directed
against the Landing Party."

日本就报纸报道提出抗议

称受伤故事完全虚假

《上海日报》（Nippo）昨日报道，关于一名中国花生小贩耳朵被日本水兵刺伤的所谓虚假报道，将成为日本向当地中国当局提出严厉交涉的主题。日本海军特别陆战队发言人昨晚对同盟社表示，已发表的报道完全不正确。如果发生此类事件，会立即报告给陆战队总部。但并未收到此类报告。

该军官声称，陆战队向上海公共租界工部局警务处和中国公安局进行的查询，得到了双方对该事件的坚决否认。据报道，一名叫陈桂英（Chen Kwei-ying）的Chapel（原文如此，应为Chapei/闸北）花生小贩，被几名日本水兵征召在北四川路和狄思威路交叉口附近搬运石头。此人因劳累放弃工作，重新叫卖货物。随后，一名日本水兵走近此人并用刺刀向他刺去。刺击未中面部，但划伤了其耳朵。伤者被送往宝军医院（Paojun Hospital，即宝隆医院）接受治疗，随后向狄思威路巡捕房报案。后者立即将此案移交中国公安局。

《上海日报》宣称，这份报道完全虚假，仅仅是针对陆战队的“蓄意煽动性宣传”。

(ALLEGED

CHINESE BY
A JAPANESE
MARINE).
At 3.15.p.m. 16-10-36, a telephone message was received
from Mr. Yorke, D.O. "B" Division, to the effect that Sinza
Station had received into their hands a male Chinese who was
alleged to have been stabbed in the ear with a bayonet by a
Japanese marine in the vicinity of Darroch, Klangwan and
North Szechuen Roads and that we could make investigations
when he was handed over to this Station by Sinza detectives,
he having been received by them on receipt of a telephone
message from the Paulun Hospital at 4.45.p.m. even date,
where he had presented himself for treatment, Dr. Chit "Cut
wound on upper part of left ear.", injury not slight, upper
part of left might fall off.

At 8.30.p.m. 16-10-36. D.S. Haskell Sinza Station
brought to the station a male Chinese named Sung Khwe Yoong,
age 46 years, native of Nanziang, who sleeps in straw huts
and alleyways in the vicinity of Paoshan Road, Chapei.
From enquiries it appears that about 9.a.m. 16-10-36, Sung
proceeded to Yangtsepoo from Paoshan Road via Hee Ka Kau
Road to a point on Tung Kyi Road, approximately 50 yards
east of Klangwan Road and 50 yards west of Paoshan Road,
Chapei, where he alleges that he was stabbed with a bayonet
by a Japanese marine. Enquiries in the vicinity failed to
locate any person who had seen the incident take place,

There are about 150 Japanese Marines stationed at the
rear of the Rokusan Gardens which is in the close vicinity
of where the stabbing is alleged to have taken place and it
is known that parties of Japanese Marines patrol this area.
On ascertaining that the offence had definitely occurred in
Chinese territory Sung Khwe Yoong was finger-printed and
with permission from the D.O. "C" Division, he was handed
over to the S.P.S. Bureau who will conduct further enquiries
regarding this case.

Japanese Inspector Hirai, on the instructions of the
Officer i/c Dixwell Road Station proceeded to the J.M.L. Party
Headquarters to ascertain if any incidents had been reported
to-day throughout the Settlement wherein a Japanese marine
had been involved with any Chinese but no such reports had
been received by their Headquarters.

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 17, 1936

Bluejacket Slices Ear Of
Peanut Vendor With Bayonet

Small Trader Attacked After Refusal To Work
For Nothing; Japanese Guards Increased In
North Hongkew Following Incident

Chen Kwei-yung, age 46, a
peanut vendor, was last night
being treated for knife wounds
on his left ear, which he alleged.
were inflicted by a Japanese
bluejacket using a bayonet.
According to the version given
by Chen to the police, the at-
tack took place at the corner
of North Szechuen and Dixwell
Roads at about 4 o'clock.
"I was selling my peanuts in
that district," the vendor was
stated to have said, "when
several Japanese Naval Landing
Party men grabbed me and
asked me to help them move
some gravel."
Case Investigated
After moving several heavy
loads, Chen decided to leave
and resume his business. He
was immediately set upon by a
bluejacket, who jabbed a
bayonet toward his head. When
the peanut vendor dodged, the
blade grazed and partly severed
his left ear.
Chen managed later to go to
the Paulun Hospital where he
received treatment. The attack
was reported to the Dixwell Rd.
Police by the Hospital officials.
An investigation was being con-
ducted by the detectives of the
S.M.P.
As a result of the incident, the
Japanese Naval Landing Party
last night posted additional
guards in the vicinity of Cha-
poo, Woosung, and Range Roads.

水兵用刺刀割破
花生小贩耳朵

小商贩拒绝免费做工后遭袭；
事件发生后虹口北部日军守卫增加

陈桂荣（Chen Kwei-yung），46岁，
花生小贩，昨晚正在接受
左耳刀伤治疗，他声称
这些伤口是一名日本
水兵用刺刀造成的。
据陈向警方提供的版本，
袭击发生在北四川路和
狄思威路拐角处，时间
约为4点钟。
“我在那一带卖花生，”
据说该小贩说道，“这时
几名日本海军陆战队队员
抓住我，要求我帮他们
搬运一些碎石。”
案件调查
在搬运了几趟重物后，陈决定
离开并继续做生意。他立即
遭到一名水兵的袭击，后者
用刺刀向他的头部刺去。当
花生小贩躲闪时，刀刃擦过
并部分割断了他的左耳。
陈后来设法前往宝隆医院
接受治疗。医院官员向
狄思威路捕房报告了此次
袭击事件。
工部局警务处的侦探正在
进行调查。
由于此次事件，日本海军
陆战队昨晚在乍浦路、
吴淞路和雷美顿路（Range Roads）
附近增派了警卫。

Morning Translation

October 18, 1936.

Lih Pao :-

THE LOCAL SITUATION

The situation at certain places in Hongkew became tense again yesterday. From 2 p.m. October 16 to last night, Japanese marines were posted on duty on Darroch Road, Chi Mei Road, Eu Yang Road and at other places, while strict precautionary measures were adopted, especially on Miller Road, Chapoo Road, Minghong Road and Range Road.
Yesterday being a Japanese festival day, the members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party were given a holiday. At 9 a.m. yesterday about 200 Japanese marines were walking along North Szechuen Road. Japanese marines were posted on duty on Range Road, North Szechuen Road and Chapoo Road. Additional marines were posted on North Szechuen Road to direct members of the Landing Party to a westerly direction.

Lih Pao (comment) :-

Yung(陳桂荣,) It is reported that because one Zung Kwei would not work for the Japanese soldiers, one of his ears was cut off.
What is the loss of an ear? Their intention is to deprive Chinese of their eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body and mind. When they have done this, they will have succeeded in uprooting the Chinese people.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

PROTEST TO JAPANESE PATROLS IN CHINESE CONTROLLED TERRITORY

At a meeting held by the Executive Committee of the Shanghai First Special District Citizens Federation at 2 p.m. yesterday, one of the resolutions passed was the following :-
"As the patrolling of Japanese marines in Chinese controlled territory is affecting business and constitutes an impairment of the sovereignty of China, negotiations should be opened.
"Resolved: that the Shanghai City Government be petitioned to lodge a strong protest in this connection."

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

SUPPRESSION OF GUIDE SERVICE ORGANIZATIONS DESIRED.

At a meeting held by the Executive Committee of the Shanghai First Special District Citizens Federation at 2 p.m. yesterday, one of the resolutions passed was the following :-
"That in order to uphold public morals, the Shanghai City Government be petitioned to adopt strict measures to suppress the guide service organizations; that the authorities of the Foreign Settlements be requested by letter to do likewise."

本地局势

陈桂荣，据报道，因一名叫宗贵（Zung Kwei，音译）的人不愿为日本士兵做工，他的一只耳朵被割掉。
失去一只耳朵算什么？他们的意图是剥夺中国人的眼、耳、鼻、舌、身、意。当他们做到这一点时，他们就成功地将中国人连根拔起。

希望取缔向导服务组织

上海第一特区市民联合会执行委员会于昨日下午2时举行会议，通过的决议之一如下：

October 17, 1936.
Lih Pao (Comment):

THE ACTIVITIES OF THE JAPANESE LANDING FORCES
S.M.C. CRITICISED

Yesterday the Japanese Landing Forces in Shanghai compelled certain Chinese residents on Dixwell Road to do some work for them. Owing to this, an incident took place in which one Chen Kwei Yung (陳桂榮), a peanut hawker, had one of his ears cut off by a Japanese marine with a sword. The accidental dropping of pear peelings and lung-an shells upon Japanese marines was regarded as offensive, but now a Japanese marine has caused bodily injuries to a Chinese resident. This cannot be regarded as a trivial affair.

In the International Settlement of Shanghai, the Chinese authorities have no Police rights. The majority of the residents in the International Settlement are Chinese. If residents walking on the streets have to run the risk of being forced by the landing forces of our friendly nation to work for them, how can the residents in the International Settlement keep calm or attend to their business peacefully? Who is to be held responsible for this state of affairs in the International Settlement?

The hawker Chen Kwei Yung is a weak, old man and is unfit to carry heavy weights of stone debris as he had been compelled to do by the Japanese marines. However, despite his pleas he was attacked and lost one of his ears at the hands of the Japanese marines. Many Chinese living in the puppet state of Manchukuo and in the districts under the jurisdiction of the East Hopei Bogus Organization have been mercilessly slaughtered by our friendly nation.

We cannot understand why the Japanese marines in Shanghai should want to do harm to Chinese residents; much less can we understand why the authorities of the International Settlement are permitting the Japanese landing forces in Shanghai to hold demonstrations and manoeuvres whenever and wherever they like at places wherein peace and order prevails. The Shanghai City Government has lodged several strong protests against the unreasonable posting of Japanese sentries in Chinese controlled territory, but the Settlement authorities have not done a thing to stop the Japanese marines from holding manoeuvres and sham fights in the International Settlement. These activities of the Japanese landing forces gave rise to rumours which excited the public. Who is responsible for all this?

（右上角印章及手写内容：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY. No. D ... Morning Transl. Date 21/10/36）

1936年10月17日。
《立报》（评论）：

日本陆战队的活动
批评工部局

昨日，驻沪日本陆战队强迫狄思威路（Dixwell Road）上的某些中国居民为他们做工。因此发生了一起事件，一名叫陈桂荣的花生小贩，被一名日本海军陆战队员用刀割掉了一只耳朵。偶然将梨皮和龙眼壳掉落在日本海军陆战队员身上被视为冒犯，但现在一名日本海军陆战队员已造成中国居民身体受伤。这不能被视为小事。

在上海公共租界，中国当局没有警务权。公共租界的大多数居民是中国人。如果走在街上的居民不得不冒着被我们友好国家的陆战队强迫为他们做工的风险，公共租界的居民如何能保持冷静或安心经商？谁该对公共租界的这种状况负责？

小贩陈桂荣是一位体弱的老人，不适合像被日本海军陆战队员强迫那样搬运沉重的碎石。然而，尽管他求饶，他还是遭到攻击，在日本海军陆战队员手中失去了一只耳朵。许多生活在伪满洲国和冀东伪组织管辖地区的中国人已被我们友好国家无情屠杀。

我们无法理解为何驻沪日本海军陆战队员要伤害中国居民；更无法理解为何公共租界当局允许驻沪日本陆战队在和平秩序 prevailing 的地方随时随地举行示威和演习。上海市政府已就日军哨兵不合理地部署在中国管辖区域一事提出多次强烈抗议，但租界当局未采取任何行动阻止日本海军陆战队员在公共租界举行演习和假战斗。日本陆战队的这些活动引起了谣言，激起了公众情绪。谁对此负全部责任？

September 19, 1936.

Shanghai Evening News (September 18) :-

GOLD FISH MERCHANT INJURED BY JAPANESE MARINE.

It is learned that Wong Sz Han(王樹漢),
native of Tientsin, proprietor of the Zien Zung Gold Fish
Shop(全盛金魚店), tenant of hut No.854 at the corner of
Pingliang and Ningkuo Roads opposite the Japanese Primary
School, has recovered from the injury which a Japanese
marine had inflicted on his left leg when he refused
give some gold fish to the Japanese marine. At noon on
September 18 Wong again called at the Police Station to
make a report on the affair.
According to information secured by this
paper, the affair took place at 2 p.m. September 16 when
a Japanese marine appeared in front of the Nyoh Zung Gold
Fish Shop(玉順金魚廠), hut No.777 at the corner of Ningkuo
and Pingliang Roads. Holding a sunflower, the Japanese
marine asked Wong Sz Han to see some gold fish. Wong asked
the marine for payment for the fish he had taken out of a
pond, but the marine, who spoke Chinese fluently, refused,
thereupon Wong returned the gold fish to the pond. This
led to a dispute.
The Japanese Authorities have expressed
their regret, but no action has been taken by them against
the marine responsible for the incident.

Wheelbarrow Coolie Knocked Down by a Japanese Marine
Truck.

Enquiries made by this paper into a report
published by the Domei News Agency to the effect that
sympathy had been extended to one Zah Shuan Khaung(石善康)
who was injured at 5 p.m. September 16 show that the report
is incorrect.
This case occurred at about 8 a.m.
September 17 when one Zah Vee Khaung(石維康), age 45,
native of Kompo, and his wheelbarrow were knocked down
on Pingliang Road near Ningkuo Road by a truck belonging
to the Japanese Landing Party travelling at high speed. The
barrow fell upon the coolie, injuring his arm, hands,
legs and testicles. He is undergoing treatment at the
Sacred Heart Hospital. His life is not in danger.
On the morning of September 18, the
Shanghai Municipal Police detailed officers to interrogate
him.

The above two cases occurred one on the
afternoon of September 16 and the other on the morning of
September 17. They may be said to be "unfortunate
incidents".

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-

REPORT OF ATTACK ON CHINESE GIRL BY JAPANESE MARINE FOUND
TO BE GROUNDLESS.

On the instructions of the Shanghai City
Government, the Public Safety Bureau made careful enquiries
into the report published by a certain newspaper regarding
an incident in which Wu Voong Ling(吳鳳玲), a girl student
of the Chung Tuh Girls School, was assaulted and injured by
Japanese marines. As the report lacked definite evidence,
it is regarded as groundless.

《上海晚新闻》（9月18日）：

金鱼商被日本海军陆战队员打伤。

据悉，天津籍人士王树汉，全盛金鱼店店主，居住在平凉路与宁国路转角对面日本小学旁的854号棚屋，已从日本海军陆战队员对其左腿造成的伤害中恢复，当时他拒绝给该日本海军陆战队员一些金鱼。9月18日中午，王再次前往警察局报告此事。
据本报获得的消息，此事发生于9月16日下午2时，当时一名日本海军陆战队员出现在宁国路与平凉路转角的玉顺金鱼厂777号棚屋前。这名日本海军陆战队员手持向日葵，要求王树汉让他看一些金鱼。王要求该陆战队员支付他从池塘里捞出的鱼的钱，但该能讲流利中文的陆战队员拒绝了，于是王将金鱼放回池塘。这引发了争执。
日本当局已表示遗憾，但未对造成此事件的陆战队员采取任何行动。

黄包车夫被日本海军陆战队卡车撞倒。

本报对同盟社发布的一份报道进行了调查，该报道称对9月16日下午5时受伤的石善康（Zah Shuan Khaung，音译）表示了同情，调查显示该报道不实。
此案发生于9月17日上午8时左右，当时45岁的高邮（Kompo，音译）籍人士石维康（Zah Vee Khaung，音译）及其黄包车在宁国路附近的平凉路上被一辆高速行驶的日本陆战队卡车撞倒。车压在苦力身上，致使其手臂、手、腿和睾丸受伤。他正在仁济医院接受治疗。生命无危险。
9月18日上午，上海公共租界工部局警务处派遣官员对他进行讯问。

上述两起案件一起发生在9月16日下午，另一起发生在9月17日上午。可以说它们是“不幸的事件”。

《新晚报》及其他本地报纸：

关于日本海军陆战队员袭击中国女孩的报道经查无实据。

根据上海市政府的指示，公安局对某报纸刊登的关于中德女校女生吴凤玲被日本海军陆战队员殴打受伤一事的报道进行了仔细调查。由于该报道缺乏确凿证据，被视为无稽之谈。

September 18, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

MAINICHI

JAPANESE MARINE INJURES A CHINESE BY ACCIDENT

At about 5 p.m. September 16,
as a Japanese marine was cutting daisies with his
bayonet near a pond in the vicinity of the Japanese
school on Pingliang Road he accidentally cut the toe
of a Chinese who was standing beside him. The
marine tendered an apology to the injured Chinese and
dressed the injury.
According to a report of the
S.M.P., the injured Chinese does not want to take
any action because the injury was very slight. The
Japanese Naval Landing Party sent an officer yesterday
to inquire after the condition of the Chinese.

NICHINICHI

FOREIGN AFFAIRS NEGOTIATIONS COMMITTEE
DISCUSS RICSHA PROBLEM

At noon September 17, the
Foreign Affairs Committee of the Japanese Residents'
Corporation held a meeting at its office to exchange
views over the local ricsha problem.
The meeting arrived at the
following conclusions:- "In view of the fact that
ricshas constitute an important means of transportation,
any unreasonable reduction in their number will put the
general public to great inconvenience. The question
should, therefore, be studied very carefully."
The members of the Committee
have been requested to submit proposals for discussion
at the next meeting of the Committee.

《每日新闻》

日本海军陆战队员意外致一名中国人受伤

9月16日下午5时左右，一名日本海军陆战队员在平凉路日本学校附近的一个池塘边用刺刀切割雏菊时，不小心割伤了站在他旁边的一名中国人的脚趾。该陆战队员向受伤的中国人的道歉并为其包扎伤口。

《日日新闻》

外事交涉委员会讨论人力车问题

9月17日中午，日本居留民团外事委员会在其办公室举行会议，就本地人力车问题交换意见。
会议达成以下结论：“鉴于人力车是重要的交通工具，任何不合理的数量减少都会给公众带来极大不便。因此，应非常仔细地研究这个问题。”
已要求委员会成员提交提案，以便在委员会下次会议上讨论。

September 18, 1936.    Morning Translation.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

GOLD FISH MERCHANT INJURED BY JAPANESE MARINE

Wong Sz Han (王樹漢), age 26, residing in a hut on Pingliang Road in the Eastern District, is the proprietor of the Chien Zung Gold Fish Shop (泉成) on Pingliang Road.
At 5.30 p.m. September 16, two Japanese marines were admitted to view the fish pond. After a while, the marines entered Wong's sleeping room, took out a wash basin and selected more than ten gold fish from the pond. When Wong asked the marines for payment, the marines replied that they had no money. A dispute arose in the course of which Wong took back the wash basin from the hands of a marine and poured the fish back into the pond. The other marine then drew his bayonet and stabbed Wong in the left leg. Upon seeing his condition, the Japanese marines took Wong to the Japanese primary school at the corner of Pingliang and Ningkuo Roads with the object of dressing his wound. Wong was not satisfied. At this stage, a foreign Policeman No. 90 of Yangtszepoo Police Station, who happened to pass by, took Wong to the Sacred Heart Hospital for treatment. In the evening, Wong attended at Yangtszepoo Station for interrogation.
On the morning of September 17, the Japanese Naval Landing Headquarters and the Japanese Consulate sent officers to the shop to make an investigation. The Japanese marine who created the trouble was also present. A photograph was taken by the Japanese officials.
Last night, our reporter visited the shop. Wong had returned home. His injuries are not serious. Wong said that when he was interrogated at the Police Station, the two Japanese marines were not there. His loss has not yet been made good.

Ta Kung Pao :-

THE CASE AGAINST OUR PAPER DISMISSED

The other day, the Shanghai Municipal Police prosecuted our paper in the First Shanghai Special District Court for having published an article entitled "Plays That Are Banned", which was regarded as an infringement of the order of the National Government for the promotion of good relations with foreign countries.
The case was first heard on September 10 on which date the Court announced that judgment would be delivered on September 17.
At 9 a.m. yesterday, the Court found our Editor Chang Chi Lieu (張季鸞) not guilty on the ground that the article did not constitute a violation of the order for the promotion of good relations with foreign countries.

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：

金鱼商被日本海军陆战队员打伤

王树汉，26岁，居住在东区平凉路的一处棚屋，是平凉路泉成金鱼店的店主。
9月16日下午5时30分，两名日本海军陆战队员获准进入观看鱼池。过了一会儿，陆战队员进入王的卧室，拿出一个脸盆，从池塘里挑选了十几条金鱼。当王要求陆战队员付款时，陆战队员回答说他们没有钱。双方发生争执，期间王从一名陆战队员手中夺回脸盆，将鱼倒回池塘。另一名陆战队员随即拔出刺刀，刺伤了王的左腿。看到他的情况后，日本海军陆战队员将王带到平凉路与宁国路转角的日本小学，目的是为他包扎伤口。王不满意。此时，恰巧路过的杨树浦警察局第90号外籍巡捕将王送往仁济医院治疗。晚上，王前往杨树浦警察局接受讯问。
9月17日上午，日本海军陆战队总部和日本领事馆派遣官员到店里进行调查。肇事的那名日本海军陆战队员也在场。日本官员拍了照片。
昨晚，本报记者走访了该店。王已回家。他的伤势不重。王说，他在警察局接受讯问时，那两名日本海军陆战队员不在场。他的损失尚未得到赔偿。

起诉本报一案被驳回

日前，上海公共租界工部局警务处在上海第一特区法院起诉本报，理由是刊登了一篇题为《禁演之剧》的文章，被视为违反了国民政府促进邦交的命令。
该案于9月10日首次开庭审理，当日法院宣布将于9月17日宣判。
昨日上午9时，法院以该文章不构成违反促进邦交令为由，判决本报编辑张季鸾无罪。

he Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, September 17, 1936

The Readers'
Forum

Frame-Up ?

To the Editor,
I have read with considerable interest the bayonetting of a Chinese school girl, Miss Wu Feng-ling, by members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party. According to one of the English-language morning dailies of Shanghai, there is considerable doubt cast on the girl's story, it being suggested that it is a frame-up to discredit the Japanese. It seems pertinent to me to enquire whether the Japanese are in the habit of such outrageous behaviour towards women or not and for that purpose I will quote from Colonel John Ward's book, "With the 'Die-Hards' in Siberia," as to how the Japanese military behaved there during the intervention in 1918. Colonel Ward, who commanded the British units, says of the Japanese:
"They treated the Czech commanders with the most scant courtesy the English officers' carriages were invaded by their private soldiers who would insolently ask what business we had in Siberia, and when did we propose to go home, but they reserved their supreme contempt for the Russian people. These poor wretches they drove off the railway platforms, using the butts of their rifles upon the women as well as the men, just as though they were dealing with a tribe of conquered Hottentots. I did not understand this behaviour on the part of our Eastern Ally, and felt that it could only be the irresponsible bullying of a few men and officers. Later I found it to be the general policy of the Japanese army to treat everybody as inferior to themselves. They had learnt this Hun-lesson to a nicety. I give two instances which are neither glaring nor isolated, but of which no doubt official record remains. I was standing on Nikolsk platform waiting for a train, there was a crowd of Russian people, a Japanese sentry was standing near. He quite suddenly darted forward and jammed the butt of his rifle in the centre of a Russian officer's back which knocked him flat on the floor in such pain that he rolled about for a few minutes, while the Jap, grinning, held his bayonet at the 'On Guard.' No Russian, though there were many standing near had the pluck to shoot him, and not wishing to mix myself up in the affair, I took no action but watched further developments. Ten minutes later another Jap sentry repeated the same performance. This time the victim was a well-dressed Russian lady. So cowed were the Russian people that this time even her friends were afraid to help her. I stepped forward to assist, the Jap standing over me, but when he saw my revolver he put up his bayonet, but continued to laugh as though it was a huge joke. A few Tommies were attracted to the spot, and Jap saw that things were beginning to take a serious turn. I proceeded to the Japanese Headquarters situated in a carriage near by and reported the occurrence. This officer seemed astonished that I should interfere on behalf of mere Russians, who, he said, may have been Bolsheviks for all he knew, and enquired whether the sentry had ever treated me so. I answered that the first Japanese that touches an English officer or soldier in my presence will be a dead man. This seemed to surprise the Japanese officer, who pointed out that the Japanese were in occupation of Siberia, and were entitled to do what they like. I had to inform him that the Japanese were acting in alliance with the other Powers, including Russia; that we were here as the friends of the Russian people, and not as their conquerors. This he would or could not understand. I ended the interview by warning him that if his sentries were not instructed to behave a little less like savages there would be an end to those sentries' careers. I later heard that the interview did good, but could not in the case of the Japanese troops do more than slightly mitigate their behaviour to the defenceless Russian inhabitants."
The outrageous behaviour of the Japanese in Siberia during the intervention in 1918 is also testified to by Major-General Graves, the commander of the American forces in his book, "Our Siberian Adventure."
Personally, I am strongly inclined to believe the story of the Chinese school girl. I am not at all impressed by the statements of Japanese officers as to the merits of the case. In fact I have had some personal experience with Japanese bayonets myself right here in Shanghai as a result of which I am convinced that the Japanese are altogether too careless in the way they flourish such dangerous weapons towards unarmed civilians. I do not dislike the Japanese but I must confess that along with the civilised Japanese there seems to be mixed a considerable number of barbarians.
Thanking you for space, I am yours for a
SQUARE DEAL
Shanghai, September 11, 1936

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年9月17日，星期四

读者论坛

诬陷？

致编辑先生：
我饶有兴致地阅读了关于日本海军陆战队成员用刺刀刺伤中国女学生吴凤玲小姐的报道。据上海一家英文晨报称，对该女生的说法存在诸多疑点，有人暗示这是为了抹黑日本人而制造的诬陷事件。在我看来，有必要探究日本人是否惯常对女性做出此类暴行，为此我将引用约翰·沃德上校（Colonel John Ward）在《与“死硬派”在西伯利亚》（"With the 'Die-Hards' in Siberia"）一书中关于1918年干涉期间日军表现的记述。指挥英国部队的沃德上校在谈到日本人时说：
“他们对捷克指挥官极尽轻慢之能事；他们的士兵闯入英国军官的车厢，傲慢地质问我们在西伯利亚有何公干，以及打算何时回国，但他们把最大的蔑留给了俄罗斯人民。这些可怜的家伙被赶下火车站台，无论男女，日军都用枪托殴打他们，就像对待一个被征服的霍屯督人部落一样。我不理解我们这位东方盟友的这种行径，觉得这可能只是少数士兵和军官不负责任的欺凌行为。后来我发现，这是日军的一般政策，即视所有人都不如自己。他们把这种‘匈奴式’的教训学得淋漓尽致。我举两个例子，它们既非显眼也非孤立，但无疑留有官方记录。我当时站在尼科尔斯克（Nikolsk）站台等车，周围有一群俄罗斯人，一名日本哨兵站在附近。他突然冲上前，将步枪枪托猛击一名俄罗斯军官的背部中心，将其击倒在地，剧痛使他翻滚了几分钟，而那个日本人则咧嘴笑着，端着刺刀保持‘警戒’姿态。尽管附近站着许多俄罗斯人，却无人有勇气开枪射击他；我也不愿卷入此事，便未采取行动，只是观察事态进一步发展。十分钟后，另一名日本哨兵重演了同样的戏码。这次受害者是一位衣着考究的俄罗斯女士。俄罗斯人被震慑得如此厉害，以至于这次连她的朋友都不敢相助。我上前协助，那名日本人站在我上方，但当他看到我的左轮手枪时，便收起了刺刀，但仍继续大笑，仿佛这是个巨大的玩笑。几名英国士兵（Tommies）被吸引到该处，日本人见事态开始变得严重。我前往位于附近车厢内的日本指挥部报告了这一事件。这名军官似乎对我竟为 mere Russians（区区俄罗斯人）出头感到惊讶，他说这些人可能是布尔什维克，他也说不准，并询问哨兵是否也曾这样对待过我。我回答说，在我面前，第一个触碰英国军官或士兵的日本人必死无疑。这似乎让日本军官感到惊讶，他指出日本人占领着西伯利亚，有权随心所欲。我不得不告知他，日本人是与其他列强（包括俄罗斯）结盟行动；我们是作为俄罗斯人民的朋友而来，而非征服者。这一点他要么是不愿理解，要么是无法理解。我在结束谈话时警告他，如果他的哨兵不被教导表现得稍微不像野蛮人一些，那么这些哨兵的职业生涯就将终结。后来得知那次谈话起到了良好作用，但对于日军而言，除了略微减轻他们对毫无防备的俄罗斯居民的行为外，别无他法。”
美国部队指挥官格雷夫斯少将（Major-General Graves）在其《我们的西伯利亚冒险》（"Our Siberian Adventure"）一书中，也证实了1918年干涉期间日军在西伯利亚的暴行。
就个人而言，我强烈倾向于相信这名中国女学生的说法。我对日本军官关于此案是非曲直的陈述完全不以为然。事实上，我自己就在上海有过与日本刺刀打交道的亲身经历，由此我确信，日本人在向 unarmed civilians（手无寸铁的平民）挥舞此类危险武器时太过随意。我并不讨厌日本人，但我必须承认，在文明的日本人之中，似乎混杂着相当数量的野蛮人。
感谢提供版面，
顺颂

September 18, 1936.
Morning Translation.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

GOLD FISH MERCHANT INJURED BY JAPANESE MARINE

Wong Ez Han (王樹漢), age 26, residing in a hut on Pingliang Road in the Eastern District, is the proprietor of the Chien Zung Gold Fish Shop (泉成) on Pingliang Road.
At 5.30 p.m. September 16, two Japanese marines were admitted to view the fish pond. After a while, the marines entered Wong's sleeping room, took out a wash basin and selected more than ten gold fish from the pond. When Wong asked the marines for payment, the marines replied that they had no money. A dispute arose in the course of which Wong took back the wash basin from the hands of a marine and poured the fish back into the pond. The other marine then drew his bayonet and stabbed Wong in the left leg. Upon seeing his condition, the Japanese marines took Wong to the Japanese primary school at the corner of Pingliang and Ningkuo Roads with the object of dressing his wound. Wong was not satisfied. At this stage, a foreign Policeman No. 90 of Yangtszepoo Police Station, who happened to pass by, took Wong to the Sacred Heart Hospital for treatment. In the evening, Wong attended at Yangtszepoo Station for interrogation.
On the morning of September 17, the Japanese Naval Landing Headquarters and the Japanese Consulate sent officers to the shop to make an investigation. The Japanese marine who created the trouble was also present. A photograph was taken by the Japanese officials.
Last night, our reporter visited the shop. Wong had returned home. His injuries are not serious. Wong said that when he was interrogated at the Police Station, the two Japanese marines were not there. His loss has not yet been made good.

Ta Kung Pao :-

THE CASE AGAINST OUR PAPER DISMISSED

The other day, the Shanghai Municipal Police prosecuted our paper in the First Shanghai Special District Court for having published an article entitled "Plays That Are Banned", which was regarded as an infringement of the order of the National Government for the promotion of good relations with foreign countries.
The case was first heard on September 10 on which date the Court announced that judgment would be delivered on September 17.
At 9 a.m. yesterday, the Court found our Editor Chang Chi Lieu (張季鸞) not guilty on the ground that the article did not constitute a violation of the order for the promotion of good relations with foreign countries.

金鱼缸商被日本水兵刺伤

王树汉（Wong Ez Han），26岁，居住在东区平凉路的一间棚屋内，是平凉路泉成金鱼店（Chien Zung Gold Fish Shop）的店主。
9月16日下午5时30分，两名日本水兵获准入内观看鱼池。过了一会儿，水兵进入王的卧室，拿出一个脸盆，从池中挑选了十多条金鱼。当王要求水兵付款时，水兵回答说没钱。双方发生争执，在此过程中，王从一名水兵手中夺回脸盆，将鱼倒回池中。另一名水兵随即拔出刺刀，刺伤了王的左腿。日本水兵见其状况，将王带至平凉路与宁国路拐角处的日本小学，意图为其包扎伤口。王对此不满。此时，恰巧路过的杨树浦巡捕房第90号外籍巡捕将王送往圣心医院治疗。当晚，王前往杨树浦巡捕房接受讯问。
9月17日上午，日本海军陆战队总部和日本领事馆派员到店调查。肇事日本水兵也在场。日方官员拍摄了照片。
昨晚，本报记者走访了该店。王已回家。伤势不重。王称，在巡捕房受审时，两名日本水兵不在场。他的损失尚未得到赔偿。

针对本报之案件被驳回

日前，上海公共租界工部局警务处在上海第一特区地方法院起诉本报，理由是刊登了一篇题为《被禁演的戏剧》的文章，被视为违反国民政府促进邦交令。
该案于9月10日首次开庭审理，当日法院宣布将于9月17日宣判。
昨日上午9时，法院裁定本报主编张季鸾（Chang Chi Lieu）无罪，理由是该文章不构成违反促进邦交令。

Chinese Stabbed

Bluejacket Slashes Man
In Leg; Officers Say
"Accidental"

Shanghai Municipal Police to-
day confirmed the story that a
Chinese keeper of a goldfish pond
in Pingliang Road, near Ningkuo
Road, was stabbed by a mem-
ber of the Japanese Special

afternoon. The condition of the
injured man is not serious. He
was treated at the Sacred Heart
Hospital where three stitches
were put in.
Details of the trouble, however,
were not available this morning
as police and the Landing Party
were continuing their investiga-
tions.
Meanwhile, no development
was reported in another alleged
attack by a member of the Land-
ing Party which was described to
have taken place on September 8
at Kiangwan Road. A girl
student, Miss Wu Feng-ling,
claims that she was bayoneted by
the bluejackets while waiting for
a bus there.
Officer Visits Chinese
An officer of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party this morn-
ing called at the Sacred Heart
Hospital, 41 Ningkuo Road, to
see the Chinese coolie who was
"accidentally" injured by a
Japanese bluejacket the previous
evening.
The man, whose name was
given as Shi Shan-kang, was
"slashed on his leg as the sailor
was cutting flowers with his
bayonet" at a gold fish pond,
near the Japanese East Primary
School on Pingliang Road, naval
officials said.
In a deposition made to the
Shanghai Municipal Police, soon
after the accident, Domei learn-
ed, Shih said:
"As I did not receive any
serious injuries, I do not wish to
take any further action in this
case."
As soon as the bluejacket re-
alized that he had injured the
coolie, Domei learned from local
naval authorities, he "apologized"
to the man.

中国人被
日本水兵刺伤

水兵砍伤男子
腿部；军官称
“意外”

上海公共租界工部局警务处今
天证实，昨天下午5时，在宁国
路附近的平凉路，一名中国金鱼缸
看守人在争吵中被日本特别陆战队
的一名成员刺伤腿部。伤者情况不
严重。他在圣心医院接受了治疗，
缝了三针。
然而，由于警方和陆战队仍在
继续调查，今天上午尚无法获得争
端的细节。
与此同时，另一起据称由陆战
队成员实施的袭击事件未有进展报
道，该事件据称发生于9月8日的
江湾路。一名女学生吴凤玲小姐声
称，她在那里等公交车时被水兵用
刺刀刺伤。
军官探访中国人
日本海军陆战队的一名军官今
天上午前往宁国路41号的圣心医
院，探望前一天晚上被一名日本水
兵“意外”刺伤的中国苦力。
海军官员称，此人名为施山康
（Shi Shan-kang，音译），“当水兵
用刺刀割花时，在该金鱼缸处划伤
了他的腿”，该金鱼缸位于平凉路
日本东小学附近。
同盟社获悉，事故发生后不久，
施在向上海公共租界工部局警务处
所作的供词中表示：
“由于我没有受到任何重伤，
我不希望在此案中采取进一步行
动。”
当地海军当局告诉同盟社，水
兵一旦意识到自己刺伤了苦力，便
向该男子“道歉”。

Sir,
I beg to report that at 5.55 p.m. 16/9/36, a telephone message was received at this station from P.S. 90 Till, to the effect that a male Chinese had been stabbed in the leg by a Japanese Marine, on Pingliang Road, near the Japanese Primary School, and that he was removing the injured man to the Sacred Heart Hospital.

Subsequent enquiries by the undersigned, C.D.C. 290, and J.P.C. 104, brought to light the following facts:-
At 5.45 p.m. 16/9/36, P.S. 90 Till, whilst on M/Cycle District Patrol, was stopped at the intersection of Pingliang and Ningkuo Roads, by an unknown male Chinese who informed him, that a male Chinese had just been bayoneted in the leg by a Japanese Marine, and that all parties concerned had entered the Japanese Primary School on Pingliang Road. On receipt of this information P.S. Till proceeded to the school in question, where he observed standing outside the gate, a number of Chinese and three Japanese Marines. On him enquiring as to what had happened, the injured man, named Wong So Hai (王樹涕) age 26, native of Tientsin, single/gold fish hawker, residing in a straw hut south of Pingliang Road, opposite the Japanese Primary School, stepped forward, and reported that he had been bayoneted by a Japanese Marine, who had since entered the school compound. Seeing the man bleeding profusely from the leg, P.S. Till requested to use a telephone, and after notifying the station, escorted the injured man to the Sacred Heart Hospital, where after having his leg stitched, the following medical certificate was issued:-
"Stab wound of the left leg, not serious, not detained".

My name is Wong So Hai (王扫海), age 26, native of Tien-tsin, a gold fish hawker, residing straw hut off Pingliang Road, opposite Japanese Public School.

At 5 p.m. to-day (16/9/36), whilst I was occupied in changing the water in my gold fish ponds, using an enamel basin for this purpose, a Japanese marine, age between 25 and 30, height about 5'4" or 5", round face, who had been there for about half an hour, came up to me and took the basin out of my hand. He then commenced pouring its contents (water and gold fish) out onto the ground, and I attempted to take it back from him, only to have it snatched away from me a second time, after I had gained possession of it. I gained possession of the basin a third time, and although the Japanese attempted take some from me, I refused to let him have it, with result that he took out his bayonet and threw it at my leg's, fortunately I was standing near a large sun flower plant and it first struck this in its flight severing the stalk of same and then recasted onto my left leg, inflicting a deep cut in same. The Japanese marine seeing this, picked up his bayonet, and returning same to its scabbard, attempted to make his escape towards Pingliang Road. Seeing this, I along with two other Chinese who were present during the whole affray, grappled with him and led him to Pingliang Road where we met a foreign Police Officer, who took me to Hospital, but first escorted the Japanese marine inside the Japanese Public School. I have never seen this Japanese before to-day, and I cannot understand why he was loitering around my place. As I did not receive any serious injuries, I do not wish to take any further action in this case.
The above is my true statement.

I am a neighbour of the injured man Wong So Hai ( 王树芳 )

changing the water in his gold fish ponds, having nothing else
to do, I observed a Japanese marine, age about 30, height 5'5",
who had been loitering around there for some time, pick up one
of the gold fish from one of the ponds. At this time Wong ( 王 )
told him he must not do this, otherwise the fish would die, but
the Japanese instead of paying any attention snatched a basin of
gold fish from Wong and threw it onto the ground, with result
that Wong became angry and demanded money from him. The Japanese
then took out his bayonet, and threw it at Wong's leg's.
Fortunately Wong was standing near a large sun flower plant and
the bayonet first struck this severing the stalk and then
recasted onto his left leg, causing a deep wound in same.
Seeing this the Japanese marine, picking up his bayonet, attempted
to escape in the direction of Pingliang Road, however we, Wong,
myself and one other gave chase and arrested him near Pingliang
Road, where we were quarrelling when a foreign police officer
came on the scene, and after escorting the Japanese to the
Japanese Public School, he took Wong to the Sacred Heart
Hospital.

I am of the opinion that the Japanese was at fault in the
first place, as he had no right to handle the gold fish,
especially after being warned not to do so by Wong.

I have never seen this Japanese marine before and cannot

September 23, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

AIRICH
· ACTION MAY BE TAKEN AGAINST WU VOONG LING

As the girl Wu Voong Ling is
of sound mind and is insisting that her statement is
true, it is evident that some one is working behind the
scenes. The Japanese Naval Landing Party authorities
intend to take action against the girl, for the spreading
of the false report will impair the prestige of the
Imperial Navy.

It is reported that Wu Voong
Ling is not registered at any school in the Niongwan
district. She had probably at the instigation of the
anti-Japanese National Salvation Association, invented
the report for the sake of publicity.

On the ground that Wu is a
resident in the Settlement, the Bureau of Public Safety
evaded its responsibility. The inquiries of the
Municipal Police have been delayed because of the
allegation that the assault took place in Chinese territory.
It has now been established that the girl had made a false
statement.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 17, 1936

Japanese Attack On Girl Is
Given Vigorous Denial

Statement By Chinese That She Had Been Stabbed
By Nipponese Bluejacket On Kiangwan Road Is
Declared Fabrication By Officials

In an effort to check the spread of "Malicious propaganda" regarding the alleged assault by Japanese bluejackets upon Miss Wu Feng-ling, an 18-year old Chinese student, on Kiangwan Road, on September 8, the Japanese naval authorities here have wired a denial of her charges to the administration of Hunan and other provinces where the reports have received wide circulation, the three local Nipponese papers reported yesterday.

Simultaneously, the Japanese authorities have asked the Chinese Public Safety Bureau to investigate the matter "with more vigour." The papers added that the Chinese authorities have not yet given a "satisfactory" reply to the communication.

Miss Wu charged that while she was walking along Kiangwan Road, two truckloads of Japanese bluejackets passed by in the direction of the City Government. The first truck, she said, suddenly stopped and several men in full kit alighted. They surrounded her and pointed fixed bayonets.

Frightened, the girl said, she tried to run through the cordon when a bluejacket allegedly thrust a bayonet towards her, injuring her left forearm.

Says Book Was Torn

She then dropped the case containing her school books, she related. A bluejacket is alleged to have reached for the case, opened it and taken an arithmetic textbook, which he proceeded to tear up.

Miss Wu said that she then lost consciousness. After regaining her senses, she went home. Miss Wu's sister, who is employed by Dr. Benjamin K. September 11, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

In order to obtain a clear account of the facts, a reporter of this paper called at the girl's home on Range Road this morning (September 10). As Miss Wu was confined to bed owing to illness, the reporter was received by Mrs. Wu, the mother of the girl, from whom he received the following information:-

Wu Voong Ling is her third daughter. She is at present studying in the Chung Tuh Girls School. The school reopened on September 7 after the summer vacation. On the afternoon of the 8th, the girl met with this adventure. Miss Wu used to go to school and return at regular hours in the morning and evening, but on this particular day, she returned unusually late. Just as her two younger sisters were becoming anxious about her, Miss Wu was seen running back in an extraordinarily nervous condition, breathing with difficulty as if she were suffering from suffocation, while her face was extremely pale.

On seeing her two sisters, Miss Wu stammered out, as if in great terror: "Ja.....Japanese.......S...... Sword". Noticing this, her sisters became extremely frightened and hurried in to inform mother. Later Mrs. Wu discovered a knife wound on the left hand of Miss Wu which was still bleeding. Mrs. Wu then began to realize that her daughter must have met with some unexpected adventure. They therefore took her into a room and when she had regained her composure, she made a brief report of what had happened to her. Soon afterwards, Wu Tse Siu ( 吴子修 ), the father of the girl, returned home. Noticing his daughter's condition, he immediately conveyed her in a vehicle to Dr. Chen Chi Yao ( 陈继尧 ) for medical treatment.

According to the doctor, the wound on her left arm is not very serious, but as she was suffering from shock and nervousness, she required rest. The doctor then applied some medicine to the wound and bandaged it. At the same time, he wrote out a prescription and advised them to give the patient sufficient rest. She was still suffering from nerves when she returned from the doctor. At times, she utters frightful shouts and would suddenly become wake in the midst of a dream. She had a high temperature and suffered from pains all over the body. She would start at the slightest sound in the room.

The reporter went to her room to have a look at Miss Wu, but found her sleeping covered with a blanket. When her mother attempted gently to remove the blanket, signs of fright were visible on her face and she immediately grasped the blanket and covered up her head. Her mother is much worried over her condition.

The facts as to how Miss Wu sustained her injuries, as related to the reporter by her mother, are similar to the reports published by this paper on September 9. Miss Wu's mother even showed the reporter the exercise book on mathematics, which was torn by the Japanese marines. The reporter noticed ink spots on each torn leaf, and was informed that these spots were caused by the overturning of the ink bottle when Miss Wu's satchel was seized from her. 为了弄清事实真相，本报记者于今晨（9月10日）前往兰路（Range Road）该女孩家中探访。由于吴小姐因病卧床，记者由女孩的母亲吴夫人接待，并从她那里获得了以下信息：

吴凤玲是她的第三个女儿。她目前在中德女子学校就读。该校暑假后于9月7日重新开学。8日下午，女孩遭遇了这次意外。吴小姐以往早晚上下学时间都很规律，但这一天，她回来得异常晚。正当她的两个妹妹为她感到焦虑时，只见吴小姐神情极度紧张地跑回来，呼吸困难，仿佛窒息一般，脸色极其苍白。

看到两个妹妹，吴小姐惊恐万分，结结巴巴地说：“日……日本人……刀……刀”。姐妹俩见状大惊失色，急忙进去告诉母亲。随后，吴夫人发现吴小姐左手有一处刀伤，仍在流血。吴夫人这才意识到女儿一定遭遇了某种意外。她们于是将她带进房间，待她恢复镇定后，她简要讲述了遭遇。不久后，女孩的父亲吴子修（Wu Tse Siu）回家。注意到女儿的状况后，他立即用车将她送往陈继尧（Chen Chi Yao）医生处接受治疗。

据医生说，她左臂的伤口并不严重，但由于受到惊吓和神经紧张，需要休息。医生随后对伤口进行了敷药包扎。同时，他开了一张处方，建议让病人充分休息。从医生处回来后，她仍然神经紧张。有时她会发出可怕的喊叫，并在梦中突然惊醒。她发高烧，全身疼痛。房间里稍有声响，她就会惊跳起来。

NIPPO

THE "EVENING POST" AND THE "HWA MEI WAN PAO"
SLANDER JAPANESE NAVAL LANDING PARTY: NAVAL
AUTHORITIES HIGHLY INDIGNANT

In connection with the report
published in the September 9 issue of the "Evening Post"
and the "Hwa Mei Wan Pao" concerning the alleged assault
committed on a girl student named Wu Voong Ling of the
Chung Tuh Girls School, the Japanese Naval Authorities,
in denying the truth of the report, state that the
newspapers had published the unfounded report for some
purpose that is at present unknown. In their issue of
September 10 these two papers reported under the heading
"A visit to Miss Wu Voong Ling" and the following
statement is alleged to have been made by the girl's
sister:- "It is true that the Japanese marine attacked
the girl with his bayonet." The "Evening Post" also
dealt with the affair in a leading article.
The report is absolutely
unfounded as can be judged by the following facts which
have been ascertained by the Naval Landing Party as a
result of a very careful investigation:-
1. It is unthinkable that a Japanese marine would
deliberately alight from a truck solely for the
purpose of assaulting a female.
2. The dinner hour at the Naval Landing Party is
4.15 p.m., therefore, none of the men could have
been out at 4.30 p.m. the hour at which the attack
is alleged to have taken place.
3. The locality of the attack lies in Chinese territory.
Whenever armed members of the Landing Party enter
Chinese territory, the Bureau of Public Safety is
always informed. The Bureau of Public Safety had
received no notification from the Landing Party that
members of the Landing Party would enter Chinese
territory at the time and date of the alleged assault.
4. The Naval Landing Party Authorities have made
careful inquiries and it has been ascertained that
not a single armed marine had left on any truck at
that hour.
5. The Chung Tuh Girls School usually closes at 4 p.m.
The alleged attack is reported to have taken place
half an hour later. As groups of students would be
returning home from school, the affair would have
been observed by some of them and spoken of to other
people. However, the Japanese Authorities as well
as the Chinese Authorities heard of the affair only
after the report was published in the newspapers.
6. The Chinese Authorities of the district where the
attack is alleged to have taken place declare that
the report is unfounded.

《日本日报》（NIPPO）

《晚报》和《华美晚报》诽谤日本海军陆战队：海军当局极为愤慨

关于9月9日《晚报》和《华美晚报》刊登的所谓中德女子学校学生吴凤玲遭袭击的报道，日本海军当局在否认报道真实性的同时指出，这两家报纸出于目前尚不清楚的目的发布了这一毫无根据的报道。在9月10日的版面中，这两家报纸以“探访吴凤玲小姐”为题进行报道，并声称女孩的姐姐发表了如下言论：“日本海军陆战队士兵确实用刺刀袭击了该女孩。”《晚报》还在社论中讨论了此事。
该报道完全毫无根据，这可以从海军陆战队经过仔细调查后查明的事实中看出：
1. 日本海军陆战队士兵专门从卡车上下来 solely 为了袭击女性，这是不可想象的。
2. 海军陆战队的晚餐时间是下午4点15分，因此，在据称袭击发生的下午4点30分，不可能有任何人员外出。
3. 袭击发生地位于中国领土。每当武装的海军陆战队成员进入中国领土时，总会通知公安局。公安局并未收到海军陆战队关于在据称袭击发生的时间和日期有成员进入中国领土的通知。
4. 海军陆战队当局进行了仔细查询，经查实，在该时段没有任何武装海军陆战队士兵乘坐卡车外出。
5. 中德女子学校通常于下午4点放学。据报袭击发生在半小时后。由于成群的学生正从学校回家，此事本应被其中一些学生观察到并传扬开来。然而，日本当局和中国当局都是在报纸刊登报道后才听说此事。
6. 据称袭击发生地区的中国当局声明，该报道毫无根据。

Hwa Mei Wan Pao (September 11) :-

THE STRANGE AFFAIR OF MISS WU VOONG LING.

According to information secured this morning (September 11) by a reporter of this paper from the family of the Cantonese girl student named Wu Voong Ling(吴凤玲), it is learned that her condition is improving. However, she still has a high temperature and is suffering from pains in the muscles, while the wound on her left arm is likewise causing her great pain. According to one of her elder sisters, Miss Wu sustained in all four wounds, each about three or four inches long and very deep; they could not have been caused by finger nails.

It is also learned that a detailed report of the incident was submitted to the Kwangtung Fellow Provincials Association on the afternoon of September 10 by Wu Tse Siu(吴子修), the father of the girl student. At the time when Liang Fu Tso, Officer in charge of the North Railway Station Branch of Public Safety Bureau, called at her home for enquiries on September 10, the members of her family informed the officer definitely that they did not intend to make any demands in connection with this incident, apart from making a detailed report of the incident to the Kwangtung Fellow Provincials Association; they would not interfere with any action the Association might take in connection with this affair. The officer was also informed by the family that the injuries sustained by Miss Wu Voong Ling were genuine and she is still confined to her bed.

Despite the information secured by a reporter of this paper from the family of the girl student, the Japanese authorities flatly deny the occurrence of this affair. When interviewed by a reporter of this paper on the morning of September 11, a spokesman of the Japanese Embassy stated that the report was untrue and assured the reporter that no Japanese marine trucks had proceeded to the Civic Centre on the afternoon of that particular day. The Japanese Naval Landing Party laid emphasis on the following points:-

(1) The dinner hour at the Naval Landing Party is 4.15 p.m., therefore none of the marines could have been out at the time of the incident.
(2) According to the statement of Miss Wu Voong Ling, the spot at which the incident occurred lies within Chinese controlled territory. As a rule, whenever trucks of the Landing Party have to enter Chinese controlled territory, the Bureau of Public Safety is always notified and a record is kept of such notifications. There was no such notification on that particular day.
(3) According to enquiries made, no marine trucks of the Landing Party were out between 4 and 5 p.m. on that day.
(4) The Chung Tuh Girls School has more than 100 students. How is it that the incident is not known to other students of the school?

《华美晚报》（9月11日讯）：-

吴凤玲小姐奇案。

据本报记者从广东籍女学生吴凤玲（Wu Voong Ling，音译：吴凤玲）家属处获悉的消息（9月11日上午），得知其病情正在好转。然而，她仍发高烧，肌肉疼痛，左臂伤口亦令其痛苦不堪。据其一位姐姐称，吴小姐身上共有四处伤口，每处长约三至四英寸，且非常深；这些伤口不可能是由指甲造成的。

另悉，该女学生的父亲吴子修（Wu Tse Siu，音译：吴子修）已于9月10日下午向广东同乡会提交了关于此事件的详细报告。9月10日，当公安局北站分局局长梁福佐（Liang Fu Tso，音译：梁福佐）前往其家中查询时，其家属明确告知该警官，除了向广东同乡会提交详细报告外，他们不打算就此事件提出任何要求；他们不会干涉同乡会就此事件可能采取的任何行动。家属还告知该警官，吴凤玲小姐所受伤害属实，她目前仍卧床不起。

尽管本报记者从该女学生家属处获得了上述信息，但日本当局断然否认此事的发生。9月11日上午，日本大使馆发言人在接受本报记者采访时称，该报道不实，并向记者保证，当天下午没有任何日本海军陆战队卡车前往市中心区。日本海军陆战队强调以下几点：-

(1) 海军陆战队的晚餐时间为下午4点15分，因此事发时不可能有陆战队员外出。
(2) 根据吴凤玲小姐的陈述，事发地点位于中国管辖区域内。通常，每当陆战队卡车必须进入中国管辖区域时，总会通知公安局，并对此类通知进行记录。当天并无此类通知。
(3) 经查询，当天陆战队的海军陆战队卡车在下午4点至5点之间并未外出。
(4) 崇德女校有一百多名学生。为何该校其他学生对这一事件毫不知情？

September 14, 1936.    Morning Translation.

Local Japanese newspapers are accusing
the "Evening Post & Mercury" and this paper of deliberately
instigating anti-Japanese feeling by publishing false reports
of this affair. We publish the following facts as a reply
to this allegation:-
In publishing the reports on this incident,
this paper acted upon reliable information and strictly in
accordance with the Press Regulations. We have no ulterior
motive.-.In support of our declaration, we mention the fact
that on September 10 we published the Japanese denial.
However, we are somewhat puzzled over this
incident in view of the fact that, although it was definitely
pointed out by Miss Wu Voong Ling and members of her family
that her injuries were caused by two Japanese marines, the
Japanese authorities have nevertheless flatly denied this
incident.
Miss Wu Voong Ling was a student in Class 6
of the Chung Tuh Girls School. On September 10, the school
authorities sent us a letter of correction which we have
already published. The same evening, another letter was
sent us by the school reading as follows:-
"Our previous letter was a request to
your newspaper not to publish a report of the affair in
your newspaper. September 10."
Upon receiving the letter, our reporter
called on Mr. Hsu Sung Shih(徐松石), the Principal of
the school, on September 11. Mr. Hsu stated that Miss
Wu Voong Ling was actually a student in the 6th Class, but
as she had failed to pay the tuition fees and provide the
necessary guarantors, she was not regarded as a regular student.
She had not formally registered with the school. He declared
that he had received a report from her family about her case;
he added that the City Government had also received a report.
According to the family of Miss Wu Voong
Ling, the school opened on September 7. When she went to pay
the tuition fees, there were no responsible persons at the
school, so she did not pay. On September 8, she did not pay
it for the same reason, and in the afternoon the incident
happened. It was not true that the student would not pay
the tuition fees and furnish the guarantee. School books
had already been bought by her.
Our reporter made enquiries at the Kaling
Oil and Paint Factory on Kiangwan Road. The gate watchman
remembered that on the afternoon of the 7th or 8th, he saw
two Japanese military trucks travelling pass the place, but
there were no soldiers on the vehicles.

当地日文报纸指责
《字林西报晚刊与信使报》（Evening Post & Mercury）及本报通过发布关于此事件的虚假报道，故意煽动反日情绪。我们公布以下事实以回应这一指控：-
在发布关于此事件的报道时，
本报依据可靠消息，并严格遵守新闻条例。我们别无用心。为支持我们的声明，我们要提及这样一个事实，即我们在9月10日刊登了日方的否认声明。
然而，鉴于吴凤玲小姐及其家属明确指出她的伤势是由两名日本海军陆战队员造成的，而日本当局却断然否认此事件，我们对这一事件感到有些困惑。
吴凤玲小姐是崇德女校六年级的学生。9月10日，校方给我们发来了一封更正信，我们已予以刊登。当晚，校方又给我们发来另一封信，内容如下：-
“我们之前的信件是请求贵报不要在报纸上刊登关于此事件的报道。9月10日。”
收到该信后，我们的记者于9月11日拜访了该校校长徐松石（Hsu Sung Shih，音译：徐松石）先生。徐先生表示，吴凤玲小姐确实是六年级的学生，但由于她未缴纳学费并提供必要的担保人，因此不被视为正式学生。她并未在学校正式注册。他宣称已收到其家属关于此案的报告；他还补充说，市政府也收到了报告。
据吴凤玲小姐家属称，学校于9月7日开学。当她去缴纳学费时，学校没有负责人，所以她未能缴费。9月8日，出于同样原因，她仍未缴费，而事件就发生在当天下午。所谓该学生不愿缴纳学费并提供担保的说法并不属实。她的课本已经购买。
我们的记者在江湾路的凯林油漆厂（Kaling Oil and Paint Factory，音译：凯林油漆厂）进行了查询。门卫记得在7日或8日下午，他看到两辆日本军用卡车经过该地，但车上没有士兵。

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated Sept. 9:

"VIOLENT BEHAVIOUR OF A JAPANESE MARINE TOWARDS A
CANTONESE GIRL STUDENT ON KIANGWAN ROAD"

Wu Voong Ling (吴圆琳), aged 18, residing in
Range Road, is a girl student of the Chung Tuh Girl: School
(崇德女校) on East Ti Yoh Hwei Road (东体育会路), Kiangwan.
At 4.30 p.m. September 8, after school was
over, as she was waiting for a bus at the gate of the Kai
Ling Paint Works (闲林油漆厂), two motor trucks carrying
Japanese marines appeared proceeding in the direction of the
Civic Centre. One of the trucks stopped near the girl
student. A marine jumped down, seized a book satchel
from the hands of the girl student and tore to pieces an
exercise book on arithmetic. When she remonstrated,
another Japanese marine used his bayonet and wounded her in
the left wrist. The girl ran away, crying. The marine
made an attempt to bayonet the girl in the back, but
fortunately she succeeded in escaping with only a skin wound
measuring about one foot in length.
Later, Woo Voong Ling hired a ricsha to her home.
Her face was pale. Upon learning of the incident, her
family at 7.30 p.m. sent her to Dr. Chen Chi Yao (陈继尧),
No.156 Peking Road, for treatment.
According to Dr. Chen Chi Yao's report this
morning, the wounds on her wrist are not serious. The
girl still suffers much pain. She will recover after
proper treatment.

The "Erh Dong Jih Pao" (儿童日报) published on Sept.8 the
following letter written by Li Tsoh Ping (李竹平):

THE USE OF NATIVE GOODS

The people of the XX nation are continuously
importing smuggled goods to various parts of China. A
tremendous loss of revenue has been sustained by the Customs,
national products have suffered greatly, many factories have
closed and the number of unemployed is rapidly growing.
All this is due to the fact that the Chinese people are fond
of using XX goods.
At this time of national crisis, the people
should fulfill their duty as citizens of the Republic for
the sake of the salvation of the nation. Economic
aggression is more serious than political and cultural
aggression or aggression by immigration. To save the
country, we must cease using XX goods. It is only
through the universal use of native goods that China can
get rid of the economic aggression, and once economic
aggression has been removed, there will be no further
difficulty.

《华美晚报》9月9日讯：

“江湾路一日本海军陆战队员对广东女学生施暴”

吴圆琳（Wu Voong Ling，音译：吴圆琳），18岁，住兰路（Range Road，音译：兰路），是江湾东体育会路（East Ti Yoh Hwei Road，音译：东体育会路）崇德女校（Chung Tuh Girl: School，原文如此）的女学生。
9月8日下午4点30分，放学后，当她在凯林油漆厂（Kai Ling Paint Works，音译：凯林油漆厂）门口等公交车时，两辆载有日本海军陆战队员的摩托卡车向市中心区方向驶来。其中一辆卡车在该女学生附近停下。一名陆战队员跳下车，从女学生手中抢走一个书包，并将一本算术练习本撕得粉碎。当她提出抗议时，另一名日本海军陆战队员用刺刀刺伤了她的左手腕。女孩哭着跑开。该陆战队员试图从背后用刺刀刺杀女孩，但幸运的是她成功逃脱，仅受一处长约一英尺的皮外伤。
随后，吴圆琳雇了一辆黄包车回家。她面色苍白。家属得知此事后，于晚上7点30分将她送往北京路156号的陈继尧（Chen Chi Yao，音译：陈继尧）医生处治疗。
据陈继尧医生今早的报告，她手腕上的伤口并不严重。女孩仍感到非常疼痛。经过适当治疗后将会康复。

9月8日出版的《儿童日报》（Erh Dong Jih Pao，音译：儿童日报）刊登了李竹平（Li Tsoh Ping，音译：李竹平）写的以下信件：

使用国货

XX国人民不断将走私货物输入中国各地。海关遭受了巨大的税收损失，国货受到严重打击，许多工厂倒闭，失业人数迅速增加。这一切都是由于中国人喜欢使用XX国货物所致。
在这个国家危机时刻，为了拯救国家，人民应履行作为共和国公民的责任。经济侵略比政治和文化侵略或移民侵略更为严重。为了救国，我们必须停止使用XX国货物。只有通过普遍使用国货，中国才能摆脱经济侵略，一旦消除了经济侵略，就不会再有进一步的困难。

A CHINESE AND A FOREIGN NEWSPAPER SLANDER JAPANESE
NAVAL LANDING PARTY
The "Evening Post" an English
language newspaper, and the "Hwa Mei Wan Pao", a Chinese
language newspaper published in their issues of September
9 a report entitled "Members of the Japanese Naval
Landing Party commit violence against a Chinese female"
The paper states that while a
Cantonese female student was waiting for a bus on
Kiangwan Road at about 4 p.m. on September 6(?) a
motor truck carrying several marines of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party happened to pass. The marines
alighted from the truck and snatched away from her a
satchel and a text book on mathematics. When she rebuked
them, one of the marines suddenly attacked the girl
with his bayonet, injuring her left arm and tearing her
clothing.
This report is absolutely
unfounded. It is impossible to believe that members of
the Naval Landing Party could have committed such an
act of violence without any cause whatever. The
Naval authorities believe that the newspapers published
the unfounded report for some unknown purpose. A protest
will be lodged with the papers.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 11, 1936

Considerable Doubt Is Cast
On Girl Student's Story

Chinese And Japanese Authorities Have Investigated
Allegations Of Bayoneting By Nippon Marine;
Nothing Found To Substantiate Charges

Chinese authorities, who yesterday investigated the charges of Miss Wu Feng-ling, 18, to the effect that she had been "bayoneted" by an unidentified member of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party, while on her way back from school on Tuesday afternoon, have ascertained that her allegation "have no foundation in fact," Lieut.-Commander Matao Okino, Japanese assistant naval attache told the Japanese press last night.

The results of the Chinese inquiry into the charges which received publicity in the evening Chinese and English-language press both on Wednesday and Thursday are scheduled to be made public, the officer added.

The Chinese official investigator, Lieut.-Commander Okino said, had been started by Bureau of Public Safety officers on their own initiative following the publication of the charges and as a result of the filing of a complaint by the alleged victim.

This fact, the Japanese officer said, was "another important factor casting serious doubt on the allegations of the girls."

No Trucks Used

Continued investigations by the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party, he said, had definitely established that there were no trucks carrying marines proceeding on Kiangwan Road in the direction of the City Government at the hour Miss Wu said she was attacked.

"Supper at the Landing Party barracks is at 4.15 o'clock in the afternoon and it is very seldom that parties of marines are sent out at that hour in trucks," Lt.-Commander Okino said. "Moreover, a check has shown that no trucks went out in that direction in the afternoon. In addition, the spot where Miss Wu says she was surrounded is plainly in Chinese territory. Whenever marines proceed into Chinese territory we notify the C.ty Government and a careful record of such movements is kept by both the Japanese and the Chinese authorities. And then there is a member of the Bureau of Public Safety on traffic duty on that road who should have remembered the passage of such trucks, had they passed."

No Witnesses

The lack of witnesses, the Japanese officer continued, is another reason for doubting Miss Wu's statements. Inquiries at the Chung Teh Girls' School, East Recreation Club Road, where the alleged victim is enrolled as a "hearer" has revealed, according to Lieut.-Commander Okino, that there are almost 100 students who attend the institution from their homes in addition to a number of boarders.

"The majority of these girls coming from the outside return home between the hours of 4 and 5 o'clock. The attack is alleged to have taken place at about 4.30 o'clock. There surely must have been other students going home at the same hour," the officers said.

"I have read that Miss Wu's sister is asking why her sister should 'frame-up' a case against the Japanese Naval Landing Party. We also would like to know why she tried" Lieut.-Commander Okino remarked.

女学生所述故事受到极大质疑

中日当局已调查关于日本海军陆战队士兵刺刀伤人的指控；
未发现证实指控的证据

日本海军助理武官奥野又雄（Matao Okino）中校昨晚对日本新闻界表示，中国当局昨日调查了18岁的吴凤玲小姐的指控。吴小姐称，周二下午放学回家途中，她被一名身份不明的日本特别海军陆战队成员“刺伤”。经调查，中国当局认定其指控“毫无事实依据”。

这位军官补充说，针对该指控的中方调查结果将于近期公布。该指控曾在周三和周四的中文及英文晚报上公开报道。

奥野中校称，在指控见报以及所谓受害者提出申诉后，公安局官员主动启动了中国方面的官方调查。

这位日本军官表示，这一事实是“另一个使人们对女孩们的指控产生严重怀疑的重要因素”。

未使用卡车

他说，日本特别海军陆战队的持续调查已明确证实，在吴小姐所称遭受袭击的时间段内，并没有载有海军陆战队士兵的卡车沿江湾路向市政府方向行驶。

奥野中校说：“海军陆战队兵营的晚餐时间是下午4点15分，在那个时间点很少会派海军陆战队小队乘卡车外出。此外，经查证，当天下午没有卡车朝那个方向驶出。另外，吴小姐称被包围的地点明显位于中国领土范围内。每当海军陆战队进入中国领土时，我们都会通知市政府，且中日双方当局均对此类行动保持仔细记录。而且，该路段有一名公安局警员负责交通执勤，如果有此类卡车经过，他应该会有印象。”

无目击者

这位日本军官继续说道，缺乏目击者是怀疑吴小姐陈述的另一个原因。据奥野中校称，对东娱乐会路（East Recreation Club Road）崇德女中的调查显示， alleged victim（音译：所谓受害者）在该校作为“旁听生”就读，除了部分寄宿生外，还有近100名学生从家中走读上学。

“这些来自校外的大多数女孩在4点到5点之间回家。据称袭击发生在4点30分左右。当时肯定还有其他学生也在回家路上，”该军官说。

“我读到吴小姐的姐姐在问，为什么她的妹妹要‘捏造’一起针对日本海军陆战队的案件。我们也想知道她为什么要这样做，”奥野中校评论道。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, September 10, 1936
16374

Bayoneted, Girl Says

Showing her bandaged arm and the torn arithmetic textbook, Miss Wu Feng-ling, 18, claims that she was "bayoneted" by a member of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party Tuesday afternoon when she was waiting for a bus near the north end of Kiangwan Road. — Evening Post photo by Mike Nenchew.

Attack Victim
Denies Frame-Up

'Bayoneted' Girl Relates
How Japanese Tore Up
School Textbook

"Why should my sister 'frame-up' a case against the Japanese Naval Landing Party?" retorted Miss Wu, sister of the victim, of an alleged bayonet attack and a nurse in the office of Dr. Benjamin B. K. Wong, dentist at 355 Peking Road, this morning when she was informed that the Japanese naval authorities have, through the Domei News Agency, denied reports of the incident.

"My sister is now running a high fever and still suffering from the shock she received Tuesday afternoon," Miss Wu continued. "Although her report was not coherent, she was able to remember vividly that she was surrounded by the Japanese bluejackets who spoke Japanese to her before snatching her bag."

Chinese Investigating

Following publication of Miss Wu's allegations, the City Government of Greater Shanghai has taken the initiative in investigating the case. Mr. Li Ta-chao, chief of the general affairs department of the City Government, this morning called on the Wu family and investigated Miss Wu's statements. Mr. Liang Wu-chu, chief of the North Station branch of the Bureau of Public Safety, also made a personal call on Miss Wu to check on her allegations.

It was revealed this morning that the principal of the Chung Teh Girls' School, with whom Miss Wu's family filed their first complaint, did not take any action. Miss Wu's father, a bank employee, is sending a petition to the Cantonese Guild asking for assistance in pressing for a thorough investigation into the incident and to demand of the Japanese authorities punishment of the bluejackets who allegedly attacked Miss Wu on Tuesday afternoon.

Girl Still Feeble

Still feeble and incoherent in her narration with a trembling voice, yesterday evening Miss Wu Feng-ling, 18-year-old Cantonese student of the Chung Teh Girls' School, East Recreation Club Road, was unable to give an Evening Post interviewer a clear story about her alleged experience of being bayoneted by a member of the Japanese Naval Landing Party near the north end of Kiangwan Road at 4.30 Tuesday afternoon.

She was still nervous although fully 24 hours had passed since she received the interviewer at her humble home on Range Road. She was noticeably shocked and rattled. She closed her eyes from nervous and physical fatigue.

Surrounded By Bluejackets

From the fragments of stories told, it appeared that she returned to school Monday morning after the summer recess. Tuesday, as usual, she left the school at about 4.30 and was walking to the bus stop to take the bus that goes to the southern end of Fatchan Road, which is near her home. At the middle of the street, she saw two truckloads of men of the Japanese Naval Landing Party heading toward the Civic Center. As she was waiting for the trucks to pass her, the vehicles suddenly stopped. A number of Japanese bluejackets, the exact number of whom Miss Wu was unable to say, alighted and surrounded her.

One of them, it appeared, tried to snatch her school bag with the apparent intent of looking over the text-books to see if they contained any anti-Japanese lessons. The frightened girl hesitated and the bluejacket produced his bayonet and stabbed her in her left arm, causing two painful but not serious flesh wounds. Finally the girl yielded.

Looked Over Books

The bluejackets gathered round and looked over the books, apparently finding nothing offending their national pride. One of them, however, took exception to the arithmetic book which, like those in English, answers all of the exercises at the back of the book. He tore the answer section from the book and threw it onto the street. As the girl stooped to pick up the books and put them back into the bag, the bluejacket tore her silk gown—white with pink stripes—with his bayonet.

The bluejackets left the frightened girl and resumed their motor-ride. The girl rushed home with her arm profusely bleeding. She was later treated by Dr. Guy Huch Chan.

Denies Provocation

Questioned, Miss Wu stoutly denied that she had in any way provoked the unexpected attack. She had not even looked at the Japanese when the trucks were proceeding her way. She just stood at the side of the street.

Miss Wu has reported the case to her principal but so far nothing has been done by the school chief.

"Malicious Libel"

Allegations of Miss Wu were termed "a malicious libel" by a Japanese naval spokesman last night, Domei reported.

"A thorough investigation, conducted following the publication of the charge, has shown that there were no marines proceeding on Kiangwan Road in trucks at the hour at which the attack is alleged to have taken place," Lieut.-Commander Matao Okino, assistant naval attache, told the Japanese press last night. "The inquiry into the allegations of Miss Wu was carried out on our own initiative since no official or private complaint has been received by us so far."

Record Kept

A careful record of all movements of armed men and vehicles is kept by the Landing Party, Lieut.-Commander Okino said. Close investigation of such documents and a questioning of the officer of the day on duty Tuesday showed that no armed force in trucks had been sent on Kiangwan Road at the time Miss Wu said she was on her way home from school.

The matter had been referred to the Shanghai Municipal Police with a request that a thorough investigation be effected, the spokesman added.
