《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年9月10日，星期四
16374

女孩称被刺刀刺伤

吴凤玲小姐，18岁，展示她包扎着的手臂和被撕破的算术课本，声称周二下午她在江湾路北端附近等公交车时，被一名日本特别海军陆战队成员“刺伤”。——《晚邮报》迈克·嫩切夫（Mike Nenchew）摄。

袭击受害者
否认捏造

“被刺”女孩讲述
日本人如何撕毁
学校课本

“我妹妹为什么要‘捏造’一起针对日本海军陆战队的案件？”受害者的姐姐、也是护士的吴小姐，今早在北京路355号牙医本杰明·B·K·黄（Benjamin B. K. Wong）医生的诊所得知日本海军当局通过同盟通讯社否认有关该事件的报道后，反问道。

“我妹妹现在发高烧，仍受周二下午所受惊吓的影响，”吴小姐继续说道。“虽然她的报告语无伦次，但她能清晰地记得，她被讲日语的日本水兵包围，随后包被抢走。”

中方正在调查

吴小姐的指控见报后，上海特别市政府主动介入调查此案。市政府总务处处长李达潮先生今早拜访了吴家，并对吴小姐的陈述进行了调查。公安局北站分局局长梁武柱先生也亲自拜访了吴小姐，以核实其指控。

今早获悉，吴家首先向其投诉的崇德女中校长并未采取任何行动。吴小姐的父亲是一名银行职员，正向广东同乡会递交请愿书，请求协助推动对该事件进行彻底调查，并要求日本当局惩处据称于周二下午袭击吴小姐的水兵。

女孩仍然虚弱

昨晚，18岁的广东籍学生、就读于东娱乐会路崇德女中的吴凤玲小姐，身体仍然虚弱，叙述语无伦次，声音颤抖，无法向《晚邮报》记者清楚讲述她据称在周二下午4点30分左右于江湾路北端附近被一名日本海军陆战队成员用刺刀刺伤的经历。

尽管距离她在兰路（Range Road）简陋的家中接受采访已过去整整24小时，她仍然紧张不安。她明显受到惊吓且心神不宁。因神经和身体疲劳，她闭上了双眼。

被水兵包围

从她零碎的讲述中可以看出，暑假结束后，她于周一早上回到学校。周二，像往常一样，她在4点30分左右离开学校，步行前往公交车站，准备乘坐开往法昌路（Fatchan Road）南端的公交车，那里离她家很近。在马路中间，她看到两卡车的日本海军陆战队人员正朝市中心（Civic Center）方向行进。当她等待卡车经过时，车辆突然停下。数名日本水兵下车并将她包围，吴小姐无法说出确切人数。

其中一人似乎试图抢夺她的书包，明显意图检查课本中是否含有任何反日内容。受惊的女孩犹豫不决，那名水兵拔出刺刀，刺伤了她的左臂，造成两处疼痛但不严重的皮肉伤。最终女孩屈服了。

翻阅书籍

水兵们围拢过来翻阅书籍，显然未发现任何有损他们民族尊严的内容。然而，其中一人对算术课本提出异议，因为像英文课本一样，该书的答案全部列在书后。他将答案部分从书中撕下并扔在街上。当女孩弯腰捡起书本并放回包中时，那名水兵用刺刀撕破了她的丝绸旗袍——白色底粉色条纹。

水兵们离开了受惊的女孩，继续乘车离去。女孩手臂大量出血，奔回家中。随后由顾惠珍（Guy Huch Chan）医生为其治疗。

否认挑衅

在被问及此事时，吴小姐坚决否认她以任何方式挑起了这次意外的袭击。当卡车向她驶来时，她甚至没有看日本人一眼。她只是站在路边。

吴小姐已向校长报告此案，但截至目前，校方负责人未采取任何行动。

“恶意诽谤”

据同盟社报道，日本海军发言人昨晚称吴小姐的指控为“恶意诽谤”。

日本海军助理武官奥野又雄中校昨晚对日本新闻界表示：“在指控公布后进行的彻底调查显示，在据称发生袭击的时间段内，没有海军陆战队人员乘卡车沿江湾路行进。对吴小姐指控的调查是我们主动进行的，因为截至目前我们未收到任何官方或私人投诉。”

保持记录

奥野中校说，海军陆战队对所有武装人员和车辆的行动都保持仔细记录。对这些文件的仔细调查以及对周二值班军官的问询显示，在吴小姐称其放学回家的时间，并没有武装部队乘卡车被派往江湾路。

发言人补充说，此事已移交上海公共租界工部局警务处，并要求进行彻底调查。

少女关于刺刀袭击的陈述遭否认

日本海军官员称该指控为“恶意诽谤”；登陆部队长官着手调查相关报道

现居虹口路（Range Road）538号11室的18岁广东女学生吴凤玲（Wu Feng-ling）小姐声称，她在周二下午被日本特别海军陆战队的一名成员用刺刀刺伤。昨晚，一位日本海军发言人将此指控称为“恶意诽谤”。

日本海军助理武官奥野又雄（Matao Okino，音译）中佐昨晚宣称：“在指控公布后进行的彻底调查显示，在据称发生袭击的时间段内，并没有海军陆战队员乘坐卡车行进在江湾路上。”“由于我们迄今未收到任何官方或私人的投诉，对吴小姐指控的调查是我们主动进行的。”奥野中佐表示，登陆部队对所有武装人员和车辆的行动都保持着仔细的记录。对这些文件的仔细审查以及对周二值班军官的问询表明，在吴小姐所称的她放学回家的时间，并没有武装部队乘卡车被派往江湾路。

奥野中佐说，登陆部队司令近藤英次郎（Eijiro Kondo，音译）少将已亲自指导了对吴小姐指控的调查。

要求调查

该发言人补充说，此事已移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处，并要求进行彻底调查。

就读于江湾娱乐会路（Recreation Club Road）崇德女中（Chung Teh Girls' School）的吴小姐昨天在家中休息。她展示了左前臂上两道长约两英寸的平行划痕，并抱怨左肩疼痛。

昨天上午为她诊治的北京路156号陈继尧（Guy Hugh Chan，音译）医生表示，伤口“表浅且不严重”。

据吴小姐称，周二下午约4点30分，两卡车的日本特别海军陆战队队员经过江湾路，前往市政府方向。她说，第一辆卡车突然停下，几名全副武装的海军陆战队员下车。他们包围了她，并举起装有固定刺刀的步枪指向她。

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated Sept. 9:

"VIOLENT BEHAVIOUR OF A JAPANESE MARINE TOWARDS A
CANTONESE GIRL STUDENT ON KIANGWAN ROAD"

Wu Voong Ling (吳圓琳), aged 18, residing in
Range Road, is a girl student of the Chung Tuh Girls School
(崇德女校) on East Ti Yoh Hwei Road (東體育會路), Kiangwan.
At 4.30 p.m. September 8, after school was
over, as she was waiting for a bus at the gate of the Kai
Ling Paint Works (開林油漆廠), two motor trucks carrying
Japanese marines appeared proceeding in the direction of the
Civic Centre. One of the trucks stopped near the girl
student. A marine jumped down, seized a book satchel
from the hands of the girl student and tore to pieces an
exercise book on arithmetic. When she remonstrated,
another Japanese marine used his bayonet and wounded her in
the left wrist. The girl ran away, crying. The marine
made an attempt to bayonet the girl in the back, but
fortunately she succeeded in escaping with only a skin wound
measuring about one foot in length.
Later, Woo Voong Ling hired a ricsha to take her home.
Her face was pale. Upon learning of the incident, her
family at 7.30 p.m. sent her to Dr. Chen Chi Yao (陳繼堯),
No.156 Peking Road, for treatment.
According to Dr. Chen Chi Yao's report this
morning, the wounds on her wrist are not serious. The
girl still suffers much pain. She will recover after
proper treatment.

The "Erh Dong Jih Pao" (兒童日報) published on Sept.8 the
following letter written by Li Tsoh Ping (李竹平):

THE USE OF NATIVE GOODS

The people of the XX nation are continuously
importing smuggled goods to various parts of China. A
tremendous loss of revenue has been sustained by the Customs,
national products have suffered greatly, many factories have
closed and the number of unemployed is rapidly growing.
All this is due to the fact that the Chinese people are fond
of using XX goods.
At this time of national crisis, the people
should fulfill their duty as citizens of the Republic for
the sake of the salvation of the nation. Economic
aggression is more serious than political and cultural
aggression or aggression by immigration. To save the
country, we must cease using XX goods. It is only
through the universal use of native goods that China can
get rid of the economic aggression, and once economic
aggression has been removed, there will be no further
difficulty.

吴圆琳（Wu Voong Ling），18岁，居住在虹口路（Range Road），是江湾东体育会路（East Ti Yoh Hwei Road）崇德女校（Chung Tuh Girls School）的女学生。
9月8日下午4点30分，放学后，她在开林油漆厂（Kai Ling Paint Works）门口等公交车时，两辆载有日本海军陆战队员的卡车出现，朝市中心方向行驶。其中一辆卡车在女学生附近停下。一名陆战队员跳下车，从女学生手中夺走一个书袋，并将一本算术练习簿撕得粉碎。当她提出异议时，另一名日本海军陆战队员使用刺刀刺伤了她的左手腕。女孩哭着跑开。该陆战队员试图从背后刺伤女孩，但幸运的是她成功逃脱，仅受一处长约一英尺的皮外伤。

使用国货

XX国人民不断将走私货物输入中国各地。海关遭受了巨大的税收损失，国货受到严重打击，许多工厂倒闭，失业人数迅速增加。所有这一切都是由于中国人民喜欢使用XX国货物所致。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 24, 1936

Japanese Say Girl's Story
Was Chinese Propaganda

Naval Landing Party Considering Taking Legal
Action Against Miss Wu For Allegations Of
Attack By Japanese Bluejackets

Officials of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party here were reported yesterday by the local Nipponese papers to be considering the advisability of taking legal action against Miss Wu Fuang-ling, 18, if she persists in accusing Japanese bluejackets of attacking her with bayonets on Kiangwan Road, on September 8.

Serious discrepancies between her earlier testimony and the answers given during her examination on Monday by officials of the Landing Party, the Shanghai Municipal Police and the Chinese Public Safety Bureau were also alleged by the press.

The girl, according to the papers, has changed the location of the assault from Kiangwan Road to Sitiyu Road.

Miss Wu charged that she was suddenly accosted by Japanese bluejackets, passing in motor lorries, as she was walking home from her school. The marines, she said, jumped off the trucks, tore her clothes, slashed her arm with a bayonet, and tore up her text-books. She further said that she saw more than 10 trucks carrying Japanese bluejackets moving in a northerly direction.

No Trucks Moving

This allegation was refuted by the Japanese officials, who said that there were no Japanese marines outside of the settlement on the afternoon in question.

They also asserted that there should have been eye-witnesses of the alleged assault, as students usually return home along that street.

The Japanese examiners further charged that in the log of Dr. Chen Chi-lao, who examined the girl on September 9, her injuries were described as scratches, not as wounds. The "Mainichi" declared that this point was confirmed by the Public Safety Bureau.

The "Mainichi" also alleged that Miss Wu's name was not included on the enrollment lists of any of the schools in the vicinity of the incident.

"Propaganda Story"

The girl, the journal asserted, was circulating her "propaganda story," with the support of the Anti-Japanese National Salvation Society.

Officials who examined the girl at her home at No. 538 Range Road, included: First Lieut. Iwao Imamura and Second Lieut. Ryuichi Itaya, of the Landing Party; Detective-Inspector W. Duncan of the Shanghai Municipal Police and Chief Inspector Toji Kasumi, of the Hongkew Station of the S.M.P., and representatives of the Public Safety Bureau.—Domei.

Considerable Doubt Is Cast
On Girl Student's Story

Chinese And Japanese Authorities Have Investigated
Allegations Of Bayoneting By Nippon Marine;
Nothing Found To Substantiate Charges

Chinese authorities, who yesterday investigated the charges of Miss Wu Feng-ling, 18, to the effect that she had been "bayoneted" by an unidentified member of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party, while on her way back from school on Tuesday afternoon, have ascertained that her allegation "have no foundation in fact," Lieut.-Commander Matao Okino, Japanese assistant naval attache told the Japanese press last night.

The results of the Chinese inquiry into the charges which received publicity in the evening Chinese and English-language press both on Wednesday and Thursday are scheduled to be made public, the officer added.

The Chinese official investigation, Lieut.-Commander Okino said, had been started by Bureau of Public Safety officers on their own initiative following the publication of the charges and as a result of the filing of a complaint by the alleged victim.

This fact, the Japanese officer said, was "another important factor casting serious doubt on the allegations of the girls."

No Trucks Used

Continued investigations by the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party, he said, had definitely established that there were no trucks carrying marines proceeding on Kiangwan Road in the direction of the City Government at the hour Miss Wu said she was attacked.

"Supper at the Landing Party barracks is at 4.15 o'clock in the afternoon and it is very seldom that parties of marines are sent out at that hour in trucks," Lt.-Commander Okino said. "Moreover, a check has shown that no trucks went out in that direction in the afternoon. In addition, the spot where Miss Wu says she was surrounded is plainly in Chinese territory. Whenever marines proceed into Chinese territory we notify the City Government and a careful record of such movements is kept by both the Japanese and the Chinese authorities. And then there is a member of the Bureau of Public Safety on traffic duty on that road who should have remembered the passage of such trucks, had they passed."

No Witnesses

The lack of witnesses, the Japanese officer continued, is another reason for doubting Miss Wu's statements. Inquiries at the Chung Teh Girls' School, East Recreation Club Road, where the alleged victim is enrolled as a "hearer" has revealed, according to Lieut.-Commander Okino, that there are almost 100 students who attend the institution from their homes in addition to a number of boarders.

"The majority of these girls coming from the outside return home between the hours of 4 and 5 o'clock. The attack is alleged to have taken place at about 4.30 o'clock. There surely must have been other students going home at the same hour," the officers said.

"I have read that Miss Wu's sister is asking why her sister should 'frame-up' a case against the Japanese Naval Landing Party. We also would like to know why she tried" Lieut.-Commander Okino remarked.

女学生故事疑点重重

中日当局调查日本海军陆战队员
刺人指控；未发现证实指控的证据

日本海军助理武官奥野又雄（Matao Okino）中校昨晚对日本新闻界表示，中国当局昨日调查了18岁吴凤玲（Wu Feng-ling）小姐的指控，她声称周二下午放学回家途中被一名身份不明的日本海军特别陆战队成员“用刺刀刺伤”，经查实，其指控“毫无事实依据”。

这位军官补充说，针对这些已在周三和周四的中英文晚报上公开报道的指控，中方调查结果计划予以公布。

奥野中校表示，中国官方的调查是由公安局官员在指控见报后，并根据所谓受害者的投诉，主动发起的。

这位日本军官称，这一事实是“另一个使人们对女孩指控产生严重怀疑的重要因素”。

未使用卡车

他说，日本海军特别陆战队的持续调查已明确证实，在吴小姐所称遭受袭击的时间段内，并没有载有海军陆战队员的卡车在江湾路上向市政府方向行驶。

奥野中校说：“陆战队兵营的晚餐时间是下午4点15分，在那个时间点很少会派出乘卡车的陆战队小队。此外，核查显示，当天下午没有卡车向那个方向驶出。另外，吴小姐所说她被包围的地点明显位于中国领土范围内。每当陆战队员进入中国领土时，我们都会通知市政府，且日中双方当局都会对此类行动保持仔细的记录。而且，在那条道路上执勤的公安局交通警员，如果真有此类卡车经过，应该会有印象。”

无目击者

这位日本军官继续说道，缺乏目击者是怀疑吴小姐陈述的另一个原因。奥野中校称，对 alleged victim（所谓受害者）作为“旁听生”就读的东娱乐俱乐部路中德女子中学（Chung Teh Girls' School）进行的查询显示，除了若干寄宿生外，还有近100名学生从家中前往该校就读。

“这些走读女生中的大多数在4点到5点之间回家。据称袭击发生在4点30分左右。当时肯定还有其他学生也在回家途中，”该军官说。

“我读到吴小姐的姐姐在问，为什么她的妹妹要‘捏造’一起针对日本海军陆战队的案件。我们也想知道她为什么要这样做，”奥野中校评论道。

THE "EVENING POST" AND THE "HWA MEI WAN PAO"
SLANDER JAPANESE NAVAL LANDING PARTY: NAVAL
AUTHORITIES RIGHTLY INDIGNANT

In connection with the report
published in the September 9 issue of the "Evening Post"
and the "Hwa Mei Wan Pao" concerning the alleged assault
committed on a girl student named Wu Voong Ling of the
Chung Tuh Girls School, the Japanese Naval Authorities,
in denying the truth of the report, state that the
newspapers had published the unfounded report for some
purpose that is at present unknown. In their issue of
September 10 these two papers reported under the heading
"A visit to Miss Wu Voong Ling" and the following
statement is alleged to have been made by the girl's
sister:- "It is true that the Japanese marine attacked
the girl with his bayonet." The "Evening Post" also
dealt with the affair in a leading article.
The report is absolutely
unfounded as can be judged by the following facts which
have been ascertained by the Naval Landing Party as a
result of a very careful investigation:-
1. It is unthinkable that a Japanese marine would
deliberately alight from a truck solely for the
purpose of assaulting a female.
2. The dinner hour at the Naval Landing Party is
4.15 p.m., therefore, none of the men could have
been out at 4.30 p.m. the hour at which the attack
is alleged to have taken place.
3. The locality of the attack lies in Chinese territory.
Whenever armed members of the Landing Party enter
Chinese territory, the Bureau of Public Safety is
always informed. The Bureau of Public Safety had
received no notification from the Landing Party that
members of the Landing Party would enter Chinese
territory at the time and date of the alleged assault.
4. The Naval Landing Party Authorities have made
careful inquiries and it has been ascertained that
not a single armed marine had left on any truck at
that hour.
5. The Chung Tuh Girls School usually closes at 4 p.m.
The alleged attack is reported to have taken place
half an hour later. As groups of students would be
returning home from school, the affair would have
been observed by some of them and spoken of to other
people. However, the Japanese Authorities as well
as the Chinese Authorities heard of the affair only
after the report was published in the newspapers.
6. The Chinese Authorities of the district where the
attack is alleged to have taken place declare that
the report is unfounded.

《日日新闻》

《晚报》与《华美晚报》诽谤日本海军陆战队：海军当局正当愤慨

关于9月9日出版的《晚报》和《华美晚报》刊登的所谓中德女中（Chung Tuh Girls School）一名叫吴凤玲（Wu Voong Ling，音译）的女学生遭袭击的报道，日本海军当局否认该报道的真实性，并称报纸出于目前尚不清楚的目的发布了这一毫无根据的报道。这两家报纸在9月10日的版面上以“探访吴凤玲小姐”为题进行了报道，并声称该女生的姐姐作了如下陈述：“日本水兵确实用刺刀袭击了该女生。”《晚报》也在社论中讨论了此事。
该报道完全毫无根据，这可以从日本海军陆战队经过非常仔细的调查后查明的事实中看出：
1. 日本水兵故意从卡车上下来，仅仅为了袭击一名女性，这是不可想象的。
2. 海军陆战队的晚餐时间是下午4点15分，因此，在据称袭击发生的下午4点30分，没有任何人员外出。
3. 袭击地点位于中国领土。每当武装的海军陆战队成员进入中国领土时，总会通知公安局。公安局未收到海军陆战队关于在据称袭击发生的时间和日期有成员进入中国领土的任何通知。
4. 海军陆战队当局进行了仔细查询，经查实，在该时段没有任何武装水兵乘坐卡车离开。
5. 中德女中通常在下午4点放学。据报称袭击发生在半小时后。由于成群的学生正从学校回家，此事本应被其中一些学生观察到并告知他人。然而，日本当局和中国当局都是在报纸刊登报道后才听说此事。
6. 据称袭击发生地区的中国当局声明，该报道毫无根据。

September 11, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

In order to obtain a clear account of the facts, a reporter of this paper called at the girl's home on Range Road this morning (September 10). As Miss Wu was confined to bed owing to illness, the reporter was received by Mrs. Wu, the mother of the girl, from whom he received the following information:-
Wu Voong Ling is her third daughter. She is at present studying in the Chung Tuh Girls School. The school reopened on September 7 after the summer vacation. On the afternoon of the 8th, the girl met with this adventure. Miss Wu used to go to school and return at regular hours in the morning and evening, but on this particular day, she returned unusually late. Just as her two younger sisters were becoming anxious about her, Miss Wu was seen running back in an extraordinarily nervous condition, breathing with difficulty as if she were suffering from suffocation, while her face was extremely pale.
On seeing her two sisters, Miss Wu stammered out, as if in great terror: "Ja.....Japanese.......S...... Sword". Noticing this, her sisters became extremely frightened and hurried in to inform mother. Later Mrs. Wu discovered a knife wound on the left hand of Miss Wu which was still bleeding. Mrs. Wu then began to realize that her daughter must have met with some unexpected adventure. They therefore took her into a room and when she had regained her composure, she made a brief report of what had happened to her. Soon afterwards, Wu Tse Siu ( 吴子修 ), the father of the girl, returned home. Noticing his daughter's condition, he immediately conveyed her in a vehicle to Dr. Chen Chi Yao ( 陈继尧 ) for medical treatment.
According to the doctor, the wound on her left arm is not very serious, but as she was suffering from shock and nervousness, she required rest. The doctor then applied some medicine to the wound and bandaged it. At the same time, he wrote out a prescription and advised them to give the patient sufficient rest. She was still suffering from nerves when she returned from the doctor. At times, she utters frightful shouts and would suddenly become wake in the midst of a dream. She had a high temperature and suffered from pains all over the body. She would start at the slightest sound in the room.
The reporter went to her room to have a look at Miss Wu, but found her sleeping covered with a blanket. When her mother attempted gently to remove the blanket, signs of fright were visible on her face and she immediately grasped the blanket and covered up her head. Her mother is much worried over her condition.
The facts as to how Miss Wu sustained her injuries, as related to the reporter by her mother, are similar to the reports published by this paper on September 9. Miss Wu's mother even showed the reporter the exercise book on mathematics, which was torn by the Japanese marines. The reporter noticed ink spots on each torn leaf, and was informed that these spots were caused by the overturning of the ink bottle when Miss Wu's satchel was seized from her. 为了弄清事实真相，本报记者于今天上午（9月10日）前往该女生位于兰路（Range Road，音译）的住所。由于吴小姐因病卧床，记者受到了女生母亲吴夫人的接待，并从她那里获得了以下信息：
吴凤玲是她的第三个女儿。她目前在中德女中就读。该校暑假后于9月7日重新开学。8日下午，该女生遭遇了此次意外。吴小姐过去早晚上下学都很准时，但这一天她回来得异常晚。就在她的两个妹妹开始为她感到焦虑时，只见吴小姐神情极度紧张地跑回来，呼吸困难，仿佛窒息一般，脸色极其苍白。
看到两个妹妹，吴小姐惊恐万分地结巴着说：“日……日本……人……刀”。姐妹俩注意到这一情况后，吓得要命，急忙进去告诉母亲。随后，吴夫人发现吴小姐左手有一处刀伤，仍在流血。吴夫人这才意识到女儿一定遭遇了某种意外。她们于是把她带进一个房间，待她恢复镇定后，她简要叙述了遭遇。不久后，女生的父亲吴子修（Wu Tse Siu）回到家中。注意到女儿的状况后，他立即用车将她送往陈继尧（Chen Chi Yao）医生处接受治疗。
据医生说，她左臂的伤口并不严重，但由于受到惊吓和神经紧张，需要休息。医生随后给伤口上了药并包扎好。同时，他开了一张处方，建议让病人充分休息。她从医生那里回来后仍然神经紧张。有时她会发出可怕的喊叫声，并在梦中突然惊醒。她发高烧，全身疼痛。房间里稍有声响就会让她惊跳起来。
记者去她的房间看望吴小姐，发现她盖着毯子在睡觉。当母亲试图轻轻掀开毯子时，她脸上露出恐惧的神色，立即抓住毯子蒙住头。母亲对她的状况非常担忧。

According to Mrs. Wu, the Shanghai City Government on September 9 detailed Li Dah Chao (李大超) to call at her home to make enquiries, while Liang Fu Tso (梁扶初), Officer in charge of the North Railway Station Branch Bureau of Public Safety, called on the morning of September 10. Letter from Chung Tuh Girls School

This paper has received the following letter, dated September 10, from the Chung Tuh Girls School:-

"On September 9, a report appeared in your paper to the effect that a girl named Wu Voong Ling, a student of this school, was assaulted and injured by Japanese marines on the West Recreation Road on the afternoon of September 8. The report is incorrect and we are sending you this letter with a request that a correction be made accordingly.

"The girl student in question at one time took an entrance examination at this school for enrolment as a student of the First Year of the Junior Middle School, but she was not enrolled because she failed to pass the examination, furthermore, she had failed to comply with the necessary requirements of this school, such as the payment of the tuition fees, the filling in of a guarantee form, etc. Therefore, she is not a student of this school. It is absolutely untrue that she used to study in this school. As regards the actual facts of the incident, we regret to say that we know nothing about it."

中德女中来信

本报收到中德女中9月10日的来信如下：

“9月9日，贵报刊登了一则报道，称本校一名名叫吴凤玲的女生于9月8日下午在西体育会路遭到日本水兵袭击并受伤。该报道不实，特致此信，请求予以更正。

“该女生曾参加本校初中一年级的入学考试，但因考试不及格而未获录取，此外，她亦未符合本校的必要要求，如缴纳学费、填写保证书等。因此，她并非本校学生。所谓她曾在本校就读纯属虚构。至于事件的实际情况，恕我们一无所知。”

The Readers'

Kiangwan "Incident"

To the Editor,
Shanghai Evening Post
and Mercury,
Sir:
With reference to the articles appearing in your issues of September 9th and 10th, relative to an alleged assault last Tuesday near the north end of Kiangwan Road, in which a Japanese blue-jacket is accused of stabbing a Chinese girl and tearing one of her schoolbooks, I have to inform you that the Headquarters of the Japanese Naval Landing Party made a prompt and thorough investigation of the matter, as a result of which it has been established beyond doubt that there was no unit of the Landing Party, in trucks or otherwise, at the place mentioned or in the neighbourhood at or around the time the assault is supposed to have taken place. Moreover, it is inconceivable that a member of the Japanese armed forces could have committed such a cowardly attack in the circumstances described, which in itself is sufficient to brand the story as a malicious and contemptible canard. Furthermore, the statement that there were no witnesses to the incident is significant. Accordingly, I have to enter a categorical denial of what is unquestionably a mendacious fabrication.
To those of unbiased and intelligent mind, who have been following the series of murderous acts perpetrated in recent months in China against certain unfortunate countrymen of mine, the reason for this preposterous story will not be difficult to deduce. Also, they will not fail, I hope, to draw the obvious conclusions from your evident anxiety and haste to give it credence.
Please be good enough to publish this letter in this evening's edition of your paper.
Yours faithfully,
"T"

致编辑先生：

先生：
关于贵报9月9日和10日刊出的文章，提及上周二在江湾路北端附近发生的一起所谓袭击事件，其中一名日本水兵被指控刺伤一名中国女孩并撕毁其一本课本，本人须告知阁下，日本海军陆战队总部已对此事进行了迅速而彻底的调查。调查结果确凿无疑地表明，在据称发生袭击的时间前后，陆战队没有任何分队（无论是乘卡车还是其他方式）出现在所述地点或附近地区。此外，在当时所述的情况下，日本武装部队成员竟会实施如此懦弱的袭击，这是不可想象的，这一事实本身足以将该故事定性为恶毒且卑鄙的谣言。再者，声称该事件没有目击者，这一点意味深长。因此，本人必须对这一毫无疑问的谎言捏造予以断然否认。
对于那些秉持公正和理智、一直关注近几个月在中国针对我某些不幸同胞所实施的一系列谋杀行径的人士而言，不难推断出这则荒谬故事背后的原因。同时，我希望他们也不难从贵报显然急于采信该故事的焦虑和匆忙中得出显而易见的结论。
恳请惠予在今晚的报纸版面上刊登此信。
此致
敬礼
“T”
